title: How to Check Your NSSF Contributions
metaTitle: How to Check NSSF Contributions in Kenya | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Check your NSSF statement through official Kenyan services, recover access and compare contribution months, employer payments and payslip deductions.
content:
To check your NSSF contributions in Kenya, obtain your member statement through NSSF’s official self-service portal or ask NSSF for a statement. Then compare the contribution months with your payslips. A payslip shows what payroll deducted; the statement lets you check the contributions recorded against your membership.

Start with the NSSF contribution calculator if you also want to check the expected employee and employer amounts. Keep that calculation beside your statement so you can compare the same month and the same type of contribution.

Choose an official way to check

RouteWhere to startUseful when
Online statementNSSF self-service portal, then “NSSF Contributions Statement”.You want to obtain your record through the member service.
Phone assistanceNSSF lists *303# for regular member services and 0704 303303 for WhatsApp assistance.You need a mobile route or help accessing your record.
In-person helpFind an office through the official NSSF branch directory.You cannot recover access or need help identifying your account.

The phone channels above are confirmed on NSSF’s current member-service information. That page distinguishes regular NSSF services from Haba Haba, a separate product accessed through *254#. Choose the service that matches the contributions you are checking.

How to check your NSSF statement online

  1. Have your details ready. Keep your NSSF membership number and the payslips for the months you want to check to hand. Use your own account credentials when the service requests them.
  2. Open the official portal. Go to selfservice.nssf.or.ke and select “NSSF Contributions Statement” under the member services. Follow the account-access instructions displayed by NSSF.
  3. Check that the record belongs to you. Confirm your membership number and name before comparing amounts. If the details differ, ask NSSF to identify the correct record.
  4. Review the period you need. Look for the contribution months relevant to your query. If you are shown only a balance or a short summary, request the detailed statement for those months.
  5. Keep a dated copy. Use the available download or print facility, or ask NSSF for a copy. Note when you obtained it so you can distinguish a later correction from the earlier record.

If the statement page does not load or you cannot complete access, use NSSF’s published phone or branch channels. An unavailable page tells you nothing about whether a contribution has been paid.

Already a member but never activated online access?

NSSF’s member self-service instructions distinguish an existing member’s online account from a new membership. They describe “Existing Member eCert”, branch approval and an encoded key, followed by “Member Activation”. Follow the route for an existing member if you already have an NSSF number.

For a forgotten password, the official member resources page lists “Recover Forgotten/Lost Credentials” and says the account must already be activated for a password reset. It also describes recertification where account details have been lost. If you are unsure which applies, ask NSSF to help with your existing membership.

Match the statement to your payslip

Check one payroll month at a time. NSSF’s employer return instructions identify a payroll period separately from the employer number. That makes the contribution period the useful starting point for reconciliation; a transaction date alone may not identify the salary month it covers.

What to matchWhat to check
Member detailsThe NSSF number used by payroll matches your member record.
EmployerThe employer or remitting entity corresponds to the job being checked. Ask payroll about an unfamiliar company name.
Contribution periodIdentify the salary month each payment covers, including any arrears or adjustment.
Employee contributionCompare the employee amount with the NSSF deduction on that month’s payslip.
Employer contributionConfirm the employer’s share separately before comparing a combined total.
Balance and interestKeep the accumulated account balance and interest separate from the contribution for one month.

If a statement does not show one of these details clearly, ask NSSF or payroll to explain the relevant entry. For help finding the payroll figures, use our guide to reading a Kenyan payslip.

Example: KES 3,000 deducted, KES 6,000 contributed

Suppose an employee had KES 50,000 of pensionable earnings for September 2026, with both contribution tiers remitted to NSSF. Applying the 6% employee rate and matching employer share in NSSF’s Year 4 notice gives:

ItemExpected amount
Employee deduction: KES 50,000 × 6%KES 3,000
Employer contributionKES 3,000
Total contribution for that monthKES 6,000

A combined monthly credit of KES 6,000 would therefore be consistent with an employee payslip deduction of KES 3,000. Check what each displayed amount includes before raising a mismatch. For contribution ceilings, tiers and historical periods, see the NSSF rates and contribution guide.

What if Tier II goes to another pension scheme?

The Retirement Benefits Authority explains that employers can apply to remit Tier II to a qualifying contracted-out scheme. If payroll confirms that an approved arrangement applies to you, request the relevant scheme statement as well and ask which amounts went to each destination. An NSSF statement alone may not show that separate Tier II record.

What to do after checking

If the months and amounts reconcile, retain the statement with your payslips. If a month is missing or an amount is unclear, write down the contribution period, employee deduction, employer amount if known, and what the statement shows. Ask payroll for the corresponding remittance details and take the specific discrepancy to NSSF where needed.

Our separate guide to missing NSSF contributions explains the follow-up process. Keep the dates and references together rather than starting again with a different description each time you ask for help.

Common questions

Is an NSSF statement free?

NSSF’s official FAQ says it provides a statement of account free on request. It describes the statement as showing accumulated contributions and interest. This is separate from any phone-network or internet charges involved in accessing a service.

Do I need a new NSSF number when I change jobs?

No. NSSF says your membership number stays the same when you change employers. Give the existing number to the new employer and check the contribution periods around the change of job, particularly if two employers paid you in the same month.

Can the calculator confirm that my employer paid?

The NSSF calculator estimates the contribution from the pay and period entered. Your member statement provides the record to reconcile against it. To see how NSSF fits alongside income tax and other salary deductions, use the Kenya PAYE calculator and the supporting statutory deductions guide.

Sources and review date

Published and reviewed on 25 October 2026. Based on NSSF and RBA public guidance checked on that date. Follow NSSF’s current on-screen instructions when accessing your own account.

title: How to Check Your SHA Contributions
metaTitle: Check Your SHA Contributions | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Check SHA contributions through official channels, match payments to your payslip, separate cover status from remittance and resolve missing deductions.
content:
To check your SHA contributions, start with the official Afya Yangu member service and compare the record for the relevant month with your payslip or payment receipt. If you cannot see an itemised contribution record, ask SHA to trace the payment. A salary deduction, a registered account and an active coverage result answer different questions.

Checking whether the deduction itself looks right? Use our Kenya PAYE calculator to estimate SHIF alongside your other salary deductions. The calculator estimates payroll amounts; it cannot access your SHA account or confirm that an employer paid the money across.

Know which record you need

SHA is the Social Health Authority, which administers the Social Health Insurance Fund, or SHIF. For a salaried employee, SHA says the employer is responsible for calculating and remitting the contribution. See its official contribution guidance.

What you want to establishWhat to checkWhat it does not establish by itself
Your account is registered correctlyYour member details through the official member serviceThat every monthly deduction has been received
A particular payment reached your accountThe contribution record or a payment trace confirmed by SHAThat every treatment or facility is covered
Your current coverage statusSHA's official eligibility checkerA month-by-month statement of employer payments
The expected salary deductionYour payroll calculation and the PAYE calculatorThat the estimated amount was actually remitted

Start at the official Afya Yangu member portal

  1. Open SHA's official website and follow Login → Members → Member Portal, or go directly to afyayangu.go.ke. SHA lists the employer and healthcare-provider portals separately.
  2. Sign in to your own member account using the prompts currently displayed. Confirm that the member details belong to you before comparing any records.
  3. If the account displays contribution or payment transactions, check the amount, payment reference and period attached to each entry. Match them to the same payroll month or assessed payment period.
  4. Keep any available receipt or statement. If you see only registration or coverage information, or cannot find the period you need, ask SHA for an itemised contribution record or payment trace through the contact routes below.

Menu wording can change. A screen saying that you are registered or covered is not a substitute for the monthly payment evidence you are trying to reconcile. Keep your PIN and verification codes private.

Check coverage separately

The official SHA eligibility checker is labelled as a coverage-status service. Its public form asks for an identification type and number, and says that a National ID or CR number can be used.

Select the relevant identification type, enter your own details and use the Check button. Note the result and the date you checked. If you are investigating a missing deduction, continue with the payment checks below even if the coverage result looks reassuring.

Before planned treatment, ask the facility to confirm the applicable benefit, access requirements and any authorisation needed. SHA publishes separate benefit tariffs and access rules; a coverage result alone does not promise payment of every hospital bill.

Can you check through *147#?

SHA lists *147# as an official mobile channel on its contact page. Dial the code and follow the current prompts for your own account. Use any result for the information it actually gives you: a coverage message, for example, does not provide an itemised history of remittances.

If the available menu does not answer your payment question, request help from SHA. Do not rely on an old screenshot's numbered menu options or assume that an SMS registration confirmation proves a later payroll payment was received.

Your payslip shows a deduction, but the payment is missing

Start with payroll. Ask for the evidence for the specific month, rather than a general assurance that the company pays SHA. Our guide to reading a Kenyan payslip helps identify the pay period and the relevant deduction.

  • The amount deducted from your pay for that month.
  • The date the employer submitted and paid the contribution.
  • The payment reference and the record showing your individual allocation.
  • The identification or member details used for your entry.
  • Any correction, reversal or adjustment affecting that month.

A useful request is: “Please confirm the SHA remittance for my [month and year] deduction of KES [amount], including the payment date, reference and my individual contribution entry. I need to reconcile it with my SHA record.”

For example, suppose a September payslip shows a KES 1,375 deduction, but the member record you can obtain only accounts for payments through August. An employer's receipt for its entire workforce would not, on its own, resolve that difference. Ask payroll to identify your September entry, then ask SHA to trace that entry against the reference. This is an illustration of the checking process, not evidence that a particular employer has failed to pay.

Compare the contribution period as well as the transaction date. If a record is unclear, ask which month the payment was allocated to. A difference could require a payroll correction or a payment-allocation investigation; the payslip alone cannot tell you which.

If you pay your own contributions

Keep your payment receipt and compare its amount, reference, member details and covered period with the assessment and record provided by SHA. Ask SHA to trace a transaction that does not match. Get the existing payment reconciled before treating a missing display as proof that you must pay the same amount again.

SHA's contribution guidance distinguishes salaried deductions from the means-tested household assessment for people outside formal employment. A salary calculator does not replace that household assessment. Our SHIF deductions guide explains the payroll side.

Where to get a missing payment checked

SHA's official contact and branch directory lists 0800 720 601 as a toll-free number, customerservice@sha.go.ke for enquiries and complaints@sha.go.ke for complaints. It also lists county offices if you need in-person assistance.

Have the contribution month, amount, payment reference and relevant payslip or receipt ready. Explain whether your problem is a missing transaction, a payment assigned to the wrong period, incorrect member details or a coverage-status result. Ask what evidence is needed and retain any reference given for the enquiry. Share personal records through the official support route rather than posting them publicly.

Once the record is reconciled, use the PAYE calculator to cross-check your expected SHIF deduction and take-home pay. For the wider picture, see our guide to statutory salary deductions. The calculation and the contribution record should be checked separately.

Sources and review date

Published and reviewed on 25 October 2026. The official public pages below were checked for member-service links, contribution responsibilities, coverage-check inputs and contact details. Account-specific transactions must be confirmed with SHA.

  • Afya Yangu: official member portal
  • SHA: coverage eligibility checker
  • SHA: salaried remittances and household contribution assessment
  • SHA: mobile channel, support contacts and branch directory
  • SHA: benefit tariffs and access rules

title: Missing NSSF Contributions: What to Do
metaTitle: Missing NSSF Contributions: What to Do in Kenya
metaDescription: NSSF deducted but missing from your statement? Check the payroll month, request remittance evidence and use verified NSSF contacts to follow up.
content:
If NSSF has been deducted from your salary but the contribution is missing from your statement, compare the exact payroll month, ask payroll for the payment and member-allocation details, and take any unresolved mismatch to NSSF. A blank entry needs investigation; it does not, by itself, establish what happened to the money.

Use the NSSF calculator to estimate the contribution for your pensionable earnings. The calculator checks the amount expected; your member statement and NSSF's investigation establish what has actually been credited. If you still need your statement, start with how to check your NSSF contributions.

1. Match the contribution month before reporting a gap

Write down the month on the payslip, the month you are checking on the statement, and the date you obtained that statement. A payment date and the payroll period it covers are different pieces of information.

NSSF's employer guidance requires monthly contributions to be paid by the 9th of the following month. For example, September contributions are due by 9 October. That deadline is not a promise that every statement query or correction will be completed on the same date.

If you are checking a recent payslip before the remittance deadline, ask payroll when it plans to pay. If the deadline has passed and you cannot reconcile the entry, request the evidence below. For older gaps, use the contribution rules that applied to those months; today's limits should not be applied to every historical payslip.

2. Separate your deduction from the employer's share

The official 2026 contribution notice shows separate employee and employer amounts. Your payslip deduction is therefore different from the total paid for you. Check what each statement column represents before comparing figures.

For a September 2026 example with KES 50,000 of pensionable earnings, the employee contribution is KES 3,000 and the employer contributes another KES 3,000. If both tiers are paid to NSSF, the combined amount to reconcile is KES 6,000. These figures assume the standard contribution arrangement and no adjustments for another period.

RecordWhat to check in this example
September payslipKES 3,000 employee NSSF deduction.
Employer contributionKES 3,000 separately funded by the employer.
Combined contributionKES 6,000 across the employee and employer shares.
Statement entry missingAsk payroll and NSSF to trace the payment and its allocation to your membership number.

For the tiers and earnings limits behind the calculation, see the NSSF contribution rates guide. Our payslip reading guide explains how to distinguish an employee deduction from an employer contribution shown for information.

Check whether Tier II goes to an approved pension scheme

Some employers use an approved contracted-out arrangement for Tier II. The Retirement Benefits Authority's guidance explains the employer application and the qualifying scheme requirements. An ordinary workplace pension arrangement is not enough to establish that contracting out has been approved.

Ask payroll for the scheme name, confirmation that the approval covers your employment and the relevant months, and the record of your Tier II contributions there. Reconcile that scheme's statement alongside your NSSF record. Do not assume the entire combined contribution must appear in one NSSF entry when Tier II has properly been paid elsewhere.

3. Ask payroll for evidence that identifies your contribution

Send a written request that lists the affected months. Ask for:

  • The pensionable earnings and employee and employer amounts used for each month.
  • The NSSF membership number recorded against you, checked against your own records.
  • The employer's NSSF registration details and the contribution period submitted.
  • The payment date and official remittance receipt or transaction reference.
  • Confirmation that your contribution was included in the submitted return, with the relevant entry or an explanation of any correction needed.
  • The Tier II destination and scheme record, if a contracted-out arrangement applies.

A receipt for an employer's overall payment is useful, but it does not alone explain how your individual contribution was allocated. Request the information relevant to your record, with other employees' personal details removed.

You can use this message:

Please help me reconcile my NSSF contribution for [month/year]. My payslip shows an employee deduction of KES [amount], but I cannot match it to my statement dated [date]. Please confirm my membership number on the return, the employee and employer amounts, the payment date and reference, and whether Tier II was paid to another approved scheme. If a correction is required, please explain the next step and when you will update me.

4. Take an unresolved mismatch to NSSF

If payroll cannot explain the difference, does not respond, or supplies payment evidence that still cannot be matched to your account, contact NSSF. Prepare your membership details, the affected payslips, your dated statement, the employer's details, and the correspondence and references obtained so far.

The official NSSF contact page currently lists:

  • Toll-free: 0800 2212744.
  • Telephone: 0709 583 000 or 0730 882 000.
  • Email: info@nssfkenya.co.ke.
  • Branch help: use the same contact page to find your local NSSF office.

Ask NSSF to check the specified months and explain whether it needs further payment evidence, a membership-record correction, or follow-up with the employer. Request a reference for the enquiry, record the date and advice received, and agree how to follow up. Keep a copy of anything submitted.

For a discrepancy within an approved private Tier II scheme, raise it with the scheme's administrator or trustees in writing. If it remains unresolved, consult the RBA complaints procedure, which sets out the internal-resolution and written-complaint requirements.

5. Verify the outcome and protect your records

After a correction or payment is confirmed, obtain an updated statement and check each affected month and amount. Keep the original statement as well as the corrected version. A reply saying that the issue has been fixed is a reason to check the record again.

Use verified official channels for membership and identity details. Do not post unredacted payslips, identity documents or NSSF statements in public comments, and do not share passwords or one-time codes. If additional documents are requested, confirm how to submit them securely.

Before making a personal top-up to cover a disputed payroll deduction, ask NSSF how the original employer contribution should be resolved. Treat the existing deduction and any proposed new payment as separate items to reconcile.

Return to the NSSF calculator to check the expected deduction. For the effect on the rest of your payslip, use the PAYE and net salary calculator and the supporting statutory deductions guide.

Sources and review date

Published and reviewed on 25 October 2026. The worked example uses the NSSF rules applicable to September 2026. The reconciliation checklist and sample message are practical suggestions, not an official NSSF complaint form or a guaranteed resolution timetable.

  • NSSF: Year 4 contribution notice, government-hosted PDF.
  • NSSF: current headquarters and branch contacts.
  • RBA: Tier II contracting-out requirements.
  • RBA: complaints and procedures.

title: Personal Relief in Kenya Explained
metaTitle: Personal Relief in Kenya Explained | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Understand Kenya’s KES 2,400 monthly personal relief, where it appears in PAYE calculations and what to check if your payslip seems wrong.
content:
Personal relief in Kenya reduces a qualifying resident individual’s income tax by up to KES 2,400 a month, equivalent to KES 28,800 a year. It is applied to calculated tax, rather than subtracted from gross salary as an expense.

Use the Kenya PAYE calculator to see the effect on estimated take-home pay. This guide isolates the personal-relief step so you can understand what payroll has done.

Where personal relief fits in the calculation

Payroll first determines taxable pay and calculates tax using the relevant bands. Personal relief then reduces that tax. It does not change your contractual salary or replace pension and health contributions.

For a simple illustration, assume monthly taxable pay of KES 30,000, one resident employment and no other relief. Tax on the first KES 24,000 is KES 2,400. Tax on the remaining KES 6,000 at 25% is KES 1,500. Total tax before relief is KES 3,900; subtracting personal relief leaves PAYE of KES 1,500. Taxable pay in this example is already after any eligible deductions: it is not a KES 30,000 gross-salary quotation.

Does everyone receive KES 2,400 in cash?

No. Relief offsets tax; it is not a separate payment from your employer. If calculated tax is KES 1,800 and no other income or adjustment is involved, applying personal relief reduces PAYE to zero. It does not produce a negative KES 600 PAYE payment.

Likewise, a payslip showing zero PAYE does not necessarily mean zero deductions overall. Check each contribution and any personal repayment separately. Our payslip reading guide explains the columns.

Who qualifies?

KRA states that personal relief is available to resident individuals. Residency is a tax status; do not infer it solely from nationality or possession of a KRA PIN. If payroll has classified you as non-resident and you believe that is wrong, ask for the basis and have the status reviewed.

Having a second job is a reason to check how your employers handle your tax, rather than treating each payslip as an independent entitlement to another full personal relief. See our second-job tax guide before comparing two payroll calculations.

How to check your payslip

  1. Locate taxable pay and tax before relief, if these are shown.
  2. Find the personal-relief line or request the detailed computation.
  3. Check the final PAYE against tax less the reliefs actually applied.
  4. If the figures do not reconcile, identify the month and the specific difference in a written payroll query.

Do not automatically subtract another KES 2,400 from a figure already labelled PAYE after relief. That would count the relief twice.

What if relief is missing?

Ask payroll to confirm your residency classification and whether relief has already been built into its calculation. KRA’s employer notice says employers should apply personal relief to resident employees. If a correction is needed, request a corrected computation and an explanation of how the affected period will be handled; do not assume a particular refund date.

For the submission process, read claiming tax relief through payroll. The tax relief guide puts personal relief alongside other deductions and reliefs without treating them as interchangeable.

Sources and review date

Published and reviewed on 26 October 2026. The examples explain current payroll treatment; check the rules for the period on an older payslip.

title: How to Claim Tax Relief Through Payroll
metaTitle: How to Claim Tax Relief Through Payroll | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Follow a practical process for declaring eligible PAYE reliefs and deductions to payroll, supplying evidence and checking the corrected payslip.
content:
To claim an eligible tax relief or deduction through Kenyan payroll, tell your employer what you are claiming, provide evidence for the relevant period and check how it appears in the payroll calculation. Sending a receipt without identifying the claim can leave payroll unable to apply it correctly.

Start with the PAYE calculator to understand the possible effect, then use the steps below to make a clear request. An estimate does not establish eligibility.

Identify the claim before submitting it

Personal relief, insurance relief, pension deductions and mortgage-interest deductions do different jobs. A deduction changes taxable income; a relief changes calculated tax. Use the tax relief guide to identify the relevant category, and the detailed PAYE deductions and reliefs guide for the wider picture.

KRA’s employer notice, dated 6 October 2025, confirms that relevant supported claims should be reflected in payroll. It specifically tells employees to provide required documents promptly. This is an existing employer obligation, not a promise that every submitted expense qualifies.

Send one organised request

  1. Name the claim and the payroll month you want reviewed.
  2. State the amount paid and the period it covers.
  3. Attach the supporting statement or certificate and identify the provider.
  4. Ask payroll to confirm receipt, any missing evidence and the processing month.
  5. Keep the response with your records.

A practical request might say: “Please review my insurance-relief eligibility for October. I have attached the policy details and premium statement. Please confirm the qualifying amount, whether further evidence is needed and when the adjustment will appear.” This is a suggested message, not an official KRA form.

Submit before your employer’s payroll cut-off

Ask for the employer’s internal deadline. Do not confuse that processing cut-off with a statutory tax-return deadline. A late submission may need a later payroll review, but the employer should explain the treatment of any earlier affected period.

Use your employer’s approved private channel. Policy and financial records should go to the payroll contact handling the claim; they do not need to be posted in a general staff group.

Check the result, not just the receipt

Consider a resident employee paying KES 4,000 for a qualifying monthly insurance premium. At a 15% relief rate, the illustrative relief is KES 600, subject to the applicable cap and sufficient tax to offset. It does not refund the whole KES 4,000 premium. The insurance relief guide explains eligibility and limits.

Compare the new computation with the previous one using the same earnings assumptions. If salary or benefits changed too, the net-pay difference will not isolate the relief. Ask payroll to show the qualifying amount and tax adjustment separately.

Handle a rejected or missed claim

Ask whether the issue is missing documents, eligibility, a statutory limit or timing. Resolve that specific issue first. For an earlier period, ask which payroll or return correction is appropriate; do not simply claim the same amount again without reconciling what has already been allowed.

Prepare your evidence with the PAYE tax-relief documents checklist. If the calculation remains unexplained, follow the wrong PAYE correction guide and retain the written correspondence.

Sources and review date

  • KRA: employer obligations, notice dated 6 October 2025

title: Documents Needed for PAYE Tax Relief
metaTitle: Documents Needed for PAYE Tax Relief | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Prepare supporting documents for Kenyan payroll tax relief: policy and premium records, pension statements, mortgage evidence and exemption certificates.
content:
The documents needed for PAYE tax relief depend on the claim. Prepare evidence showing who paid, what the payment relates to, the amount and period, and why it qualifies. A bank debit alone may prove payment without proving tax eligibility.

This is a practical preparation checklist, not a universal official application form. KRA requires supported claims; your employer or provider may need further records for your circumstances. Use the PAYE calculator to estimate the effect only after establishing the qualifying inputs.

Prepare a simple cover sheet

List your employee identifier, claim type, provider, period, amount and the documents attached. State whether payroll has already allowed any part of the claim. Keep original documents and send legible copies through your employer’s approved channel.

For example, a premium statement covering January to December should not be presented as though the entire annual amount were a single monthly premium. Highlight the period and ask how payroll will allocate it.

Evidence to gather for each claim

ClaimUseful supporting recordsWhat needs checking
Insurance reliefPolicy schedule, insurer’s premium statement and proof of payment where needed.Policy type, insured person, qualifying premiums and payment period.
Registered pension contributionsScheme details and contribution statements, plus payroll records for amounts already deducted.Registration, employee contributions and applicable combined limits.
Mortgage interestLender’s interest statement, loan details and information supporting qualifying residential use.Interest rather than capital repayments, lender eligibility and occupation conditions.
Post-retirement medical fundFund details and contribution statement.Qualifying fund, actual contributions and statutory limit.
Disability income-tax exemptionThe valid income-tax exemption certificate and any details needed to verify it.Certificate validity and the period to which the exemption applies.

The table lists records to prepare, rather than claiming every document has an identical prescribed format. Ask the relevant provider for a tax-purpose statement if the ordinary account statement does not separate the necessary amounts.

Three common gaps to fix

Payment without policy details: an insurance debit may not show the covered person or policy terms. Pair it with the schedule or provider statement. Read the insurance relief rules before assuming a premium qualifies.

Total mortgage repayment without interest: obtain the interest breakdown. Principal repayment is a different figure. The mortgage-interest deduction guide explains the distinction.

Registration without an exemption certificate: for disability tax exemption, KRA tells employed certificate holders to present their income-tax exemption certificates to employers, who can verify validity. Do not assume another registration document alone completes the payroll claim.

Match documents to the payslip

After submission, record the month payroll processed the claim and the amount accepted. Compare it with your cover sheet. If only part was allowed, ask whether a limit, overlapping contribution or missing evidence explains the difference.

Store the submitted copy, acknowledgement and corrected computation together. This makes later reconciliation easier and reduces the risk of presenting an amount as unclaimed when payroll has already recognised it.

What to send next

Use the payroll claim process for a practical submission sequence. The tax relief supporting guide connects the individual rules. For exemption claims, consult KRA’s disability exemption notice and confirm the certificate with payroll.

title: Is Overtime Taxable in Kenya?
metaTitle: Is Overtime Taxable in Kenya? | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Understand how overtime affects Kenyan PAYE, why there is no separate overtime rate, and how to check the extra tax and take-home amount.
content:
Yes. Overtime is taxable employment income in Kenya. KRA expressly includes overtime in cash pay subject to PAYE. An overtime entry is not tax-free simply because you earned it outside normal working hours or received it separately from your salary.

Use the PAYE calculator to understand the ordinary salary calculation. For overtime, compare payroll with and without the extra earnings, checking the applicable contribution bases as well as tax.

Is overtime taxed at a special rate?

There is no universal flat overtime tax rate. PAYE uses progressive income bands. The extra taxable income can fall within one band or cross a boundary. A colleague with a different salary or set of deductions may therefore keep a different proportion of the same gross overtime payment.

Older search results can be misleading: KRA's cash-allowances guidance explains that the former exemption for overtime and bonuses paid to employees in the lowest salary bracket was removed by the Finance Act 2020. A low earner may still have no PAYE after applicable relief, but that is different from overtime itself being exempt.

A worked example of the extra PAYE

Suppose monthly taxable pay, after allowable deductions, rises from KES 30,000 to KES 35,000. These are taxable-income inputs, not gross salaries. Assume a resident employee with the standard personal relief and no additional reliefs.

CalculationBefore overtimeAfter overtime
Taxable pay30,00035,000
Tax before relief3,900.005,283.35
Personal relief2,400.002,400.00
PAYE1,500.002,883.35

The KES 5,000 increase in taxable pay adds KES 1,383.35 PAYE. Part falls in the 25% band and part in the 30% band. This isolates income tax; it does not establish the final cash from KES 5,000 gross overtime, because contributions can also affect taxable pay and net pay.

Check the hours before checking the tax

Separate two questions: what overtime you are owed, and what tax applies to the amount paid. Compare approved hours, the agreed hourly basis and the applicable employment terms with the gross overtime line. Tax accuracy cannot fix missing hours or an incorrect gross payment.

Keep your approved timesheet and compare it with the earnings and deductions on your payslip. Ask payroll to explain any difference before trying to reproduce its tax result.

Why the bank payment may rise by less

PAYE is only one deduction. Ask which portion of the overtime enters each statutory contribution base and whether a ceiling applies. Do not deduct every headline percentage mechanically, or claim personal relief twice because an extra payment has a separate payslip.

For the underlying sequence, read how PAYE is calculated. The employment situations guide also covers other changes to ordinary pay.

What if the overtime relates to an earlier period?

Give payroll the dates the work was performed, not just the payment date. A correction covering earlier tax years needs period-specific treatment. See salary arrears and PAYE before putting a historical lump sum into a current monthly estimate.

title: Are Salary Allowances Taxable in Kenya?
metaTitle: Are Salary Allowances Taxable in Kenya? | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Check Kenyan PAYE treatment of cash house, commuter and medical allowances, distinguish reimbursements, and avoid double-counting salary components.
content:
Cash salary allowances are generally taxable in Kenya. Describing part of your pay as a house, commuter, telephone or medical allowance does not by itself remove it from PAYE. The purpose and legal treatment of the payment matter more than its label.

Enter the total relevant cash salary in the PAYE calculator, including taxable allowances. First check whether the stated gross figure already contains them: adding the same allowance twice overstates both earnings and deductions.

Which common allowances are taxable?

PaymentWhat to check
Cash house allowanceNormally part of cash employment income; distinguish it from employer-provided housing.
Regular commuter allowanceCash paid for ordinary commuting is not automatically a business-expense reimbursement.
Cash medical allowanceDo not assume the treatment of employer-provided medical cover applies to cash paid to you.
Telephone or entertainment allowanceA fixed cash salary component needs to be distinguished from a supported business expense.

KRA's guidance on cash allowances and its employer PAYE guide explain the distinction between remuneration and reimbursement. The older guide is useful for classification; its historical rates and limits should not be used for a current calculation.

When is a reimbursement different?

Repaying an employee for a qualifying expense incurred in performing their work is different from giving them a general spending allowance. Keep the business purpose, dates, approval and receipts or other supporting evidence. A receipt alone does not establish that a personal cost was incurred wholly for employment.

For mileage, KRA's current PAYE page says reimbursement above AA Kenya rates is taxable on the employee. Do not assume that calling a payment “mileage” makes any amount exempt. Travel and subsistence arrangements require their own applicable conditions and evidence; this article does not set a universal tax-free daily allowance.

Example: an allowance already inside gross salary

An offer states KES 70,000 basic salary, KES 20,000 house allowance and KES 10,000 commuter allowance, giving KES 100,000 gross cash pay. The starting total is KES 100,000, not KES 130,000. Neither cash allowance disappears merely because it has its own line on the payslip.

Payroll then applies relevant contributions, allowable deductions and tax reliefs. The difference between gross and taxable pay explains why KES 100,000 gross is not necessarily KES 100,000 taxable income.

Cash allowances and benefits in kind are different

A company house or car can create taxable value without giving you cash. A cash allowance gives you cash remuneration. Do not apply a company-car valuation formula to a cash transport allowance or subtract a non-cash benefit's entire value from cash earnings as if it were a payment already received.

Use the benefits-in-kind guide for that separate question, alongside the employment situations guide.

Questions to send payroll before accepting a package

  • Is the quoted salary basic pay or the full gross package?
  • Which allowances are fixed cash remuneration?
  • Which payments require actual business expenses and supporting records?
  • How is each item treated for PAYE and each statutory contribution?
  • Does the written offer match the payroll breakdown?

Request a worked payslip using your actual package. Renaming existing salary as an allowance is not, on its own, a tax saving. If a promised net figure differs from the calculation, resolve the assumptions in writing before relying on it.

For a medical line specifically, trace the premium from your employer to the insurer.

For a journey-by-journey check, reconcile your mileage reimbursement against approved kilometres and the tax comparison rate.

title: Salary Arrears and PAYE in Kenya
metaTitle: Salary Arrears and PAYE in Kenya | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Understand PAYE on backdated salary, separate the years earned, reconcile tax already paid and request the records needed for a payroll correction.
content:
Salary arrears are pay for an earlier period that is paid later. They can arise from a backdated pay rise, omitted salary or a payroll correction. They remain employment income; paying several months together does not turn them into a tax-free gift.

The PAYE calculator helps you check ordinary current monthly salary. It does not allocate a historical lump sum across tax years. Ask payroll for that allocation before using a monthly estimate to challenge an arrears deduction.

Start with the period earned

KRA's lump-sum guidance explains that employment income received in a different year from the year earned is attributed to the relevant earning year. It describes recalculating that year's taxable income and allowing for tax already paid. Its worked examples use historical figures, so copy the method only where applicable, not the old tax bands.

Separate current salary, current-year arrears and amounts earned in earlier years. Very old arrears and payments after employment has ended can engage special allocation rules. Ask payroll to identify the applicable provision and years rather than distributing every settlement equally across five years.

Build an arrears schedule

Suppose a pay rise of KES 5,000 a month takes effect from November 2025 but the November 2025 to February 2026 difference is paid in March 2026. The gross arrears total KES 20,000:

Earning periodGross difference
November–December 20252 × 5,000 = 10,000
January–February 20262 × 5,000 = 10,000
Total arrears20,000

This schedule identifies when the money was earned; it is not a tax computation. Payroll still needs the relevant earnings, contribution treatment, deductions, reliefs and PAYE already accounted for. The payment date alone does not supply those inputs.

How to understand the extra tax

Request a before-and-after calculation for each affected year: original taxable income, additional taxable amount, revised tax liability, reliefs and tax already paid. A hypothetical revised liability of KES 84,000 against KES 78,000 already paid leaves KES 6,000 to reconcile. Those illustrative figures explain subtraction, not the tax due on the KES 20,000 example above.

Personal relief should not be duplicated merely because the arrears arrive as a separate transfer. Nor should the entire original tax bill be charged again without crediting the PAYE already accounted for.

Documents to request from payroll

  • The pay-rise letter, award or correction explaining entitlement and effective date.
  • A month-by-month gross arrears schedule.
  • The tax calculation for each affected period, with rates and reliefs identified.
  • The treatment of statutory contributions and any employee deductions.
  • The payslip, payment confirmation and relevant P9 records, including corrections where needed.

Keep original and revised documents so the change is traceable. A bank transfer proves the amount received; it does not explain its allocation or prove that the tax calculation is correct.

What if you have already filed a return?

Compare the payroll correction with the figures previously reported before making another claim or entry. Ask payroll or KRA which return period needs correction and how the tax credit is recorded. Do not simply add the same income to both years or assume every backdated payment produces a refund.

Follow the PAYE correction checklist if the explanation is incomplete. For amounts paid on exit, separate salary arrears from the other items in the terminal-dues guide. The employment situations guide connects these different payroll events.

title: How to Set Up Payroll in Kenya
metaTitle: How to Set Up Payroll in Kenya | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Set up Kenyan payroll from employer registrations to the first pay run, approvals, statutory payments and a clear monthly reconciliation.
content:
Setting up payroll in Kenya means building a repeatable process for calculating earnings, paying employees and accounting for statutory deductions. A spreadsheet that produces a net salary is only one part of that process. Before the first pay run, confirm employer registrations, employee details, calculation rules, approvals and payment responsibilities.

Start with the employer cost calculator to budget gross salary and the employer-funded contributions it includes. Use the Kenyan employer payroll guide for the broader compliance framework.

1. Confirm the employer accounts

KRA requires a person paying employee emoluments to register for the PAYE obligation. Check that the correct employer PIN and obligation are active; an employee's personal PIN is not the employer account.

Set up the relevant NSSF and SHA employer access separately. NSSF's official employer service distinguishes new registration from activation of an existing employer. SHA's corporate registration page asks for a KRA PIN certificate and business registration certificate or Act of Parliament. Follow the current official workflow and keep the organisation's account recovery details accessible to authorised staff.

2. Define the pay rules before entering figures

Record the pay frequency, contractual salary, allowances, benefits, start date and payroll cut-off. Decide who approves overtime, unpaid leave, salary changes and corrections. The cut-off is an internal processing date; it does not replace a statutory filing or payment deadline.

Separate cash allowances from benefits in kind and supported business reimbursements. Use the cash allowances guide when deciding what belongs in gross pay. Never enter the quoted gross package and then add allowances already included in it.

3. Build and review the calculation

Your payroll register should show gross cash earnings, taxable benefits, each statutory contribution, allowable tax deductions, reliefs, PAYE and other authorised deductions. Keep employer contributions in separate columns so they cannot accidentally reduce employee take-home pay.

KRA's employer guidance requires applicable supported deductions, reliefs and exemptions to be reflected in payroll. Collect evidence before applying a claim and review its effective period. A tax deduction and a tax relief are different steps in the calculation.

4. Reconcile a test run before paying

For a simple control example, suppose gross cash pay is KES 100,000 and total employee deductions are KES 29,558.35. The bank payment must be KES 70,441.65. If separately calculated employer-funded costs are KES 7,500, the combined salary-and-contribution funding subtotal is KES 107,500. This reconciliation illustrates accounting relationships, not a universal deduction schedule.

Use the employer cost breakdown to understand what is included and what additional employment costs need a separate budget. Have another authorised person review joiners, changed bank details and unusual payments before release.

5. Close each month completely

  1. Approve the final payroll and issue individual payslips securely.
  2. Pay net salaries using the approved payment details.
  3. File each required return and remit the relevant deductions and employer amounts.
  4. Save submission acknowledgements and payment evidence separately.
  5. Reconcile the payroll, bank payments and agency records; investigate unmatched amounts.

KRA sets both PAYE filing and payment by the ninth day of the following month. Track each other obligation using its own current deadline. Follow the PAYE filing guide for the return stage, and keep a documented backup person for absences.

title: New Employee Payroll Checklist: Kenya
metaTitle: New Employee Payroll Checklist: Kenya | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Prepare a Kenyan employee’s first payroll with the right identifiers, pay terms, relief documents, bank checks and first-payslip reconciliation.
content:
A new employee payroll checklist should establish who is being paid, what they are owed and which payroll rules apply before the first salary is approved. Missing information is easier to resolve before the cut-off than after a payment has gone to the wrong account or a contribution has been filed under the wrong identifier.

Use the employer cost calculator to check the budget for the agreed gross salary. This checklist covers onboarding one employee; the employer payroll guide covers the continuing process.

Confirm identity and the employment terms

  • Employee name and identity details matching the supporting documents.
  • KRA PIN and the employee's existing NSSF and SHA registration details.
  • Signed employment terms, start date and payroll period.
  • Basic salary, cash allowances, benefits and whether the quoted figure is gross or net.
  • Approved salary-payment details and a reliable private contact channel.

Check identifiers directly against the employee's records rather than guessing from a previous payroll entry. Do not create a duplicate membership simply because someone has changed employers. Resolve mismatches through the relevant agency's official service.

Ask about tax treatment and supported claims

Establish tax residence and whether there is concurrent employment or another employer paying in the same period. These facts can affect the calculation and prevent relief being duplicated. Ask for relevant previous-employment records where needed to reconcile the year, without assuming a past payslip is a template for the new salary.

KRA's employer notice requires relevant deductions, reliefs and exemptions to be applied, with supporting documentation where required. Use the tax-relief documents checklist to collect the evidence, including validity dates for an exemption certificate. Do not treat an unsupported statement that an expense is deductible as approval.

Resolve the first partial month explicitly

If someone joins part-way through a month, record the contractual or applicable basis for calculating that month's earnings. Do not silently alternate between calendar days and working days. Have the employee's start date and approved amount checked before deductions are calculated.

For example, if an approved employment arrangement produces KES 30,000 gross for the first period and KES 60,000 for a full later month, keep both figures in the record. Do not enter KES 60,000 into the first run simply because it is the standard monthly salary. This example does not prescribe a universal proration formula.

Check deductions and payment details independently

Identify the treatment of benefits, pension contributions, loan repayments and other authorised deductions individually. A deduction reducing the bank payment is not automatically an allowable deduction for PAYE. Confirm any HELB repayment instruction through the appropriate employer process rather than inventing a percentage.

Use a second-person check for bank details and any last-minute change. Restrict access to payroll documents and use the employer's approved secure channel; a general team chat is not a suitable place for identity or financial records.

Review the first payslip with the employee

  1. Match the pay period, start date and gross earnings to the approved terms.
  2. Check deductions, benefits and reliefs against the supporting records.
  3. Reconcile gross cash pay less deductions to the bank amount.
  4. Explain how the employee can check contribution credits after remittance.
  5. Document and resolve any correction rather than overwriting the original result.

Share the payslip reading guide and, for a move between jobs, the changing-employer PAYE checklist. Mark onboarding complete only when the employee is included in the appropriate payroll and statutory records.

title: Payroll Records Kenyan Employers Need
metaTitle: Payroll Records Kenyan Employers Need | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Organise payroll calculations, payslips, approvals, returns and payment evidence in Kenya, with retention checks and a clear correction trail.
content:
Good payroll records let an employer explain how a salary was agreed, calculated, paid and reported. A folder of payslips alone cannot show that statutory deductions reached the relevant agency. Keep the evidence behind the calculation as well as the final documents.

Use the employer cost calculator as a budgeting cross-check, then retain the actual payroll calculation used. A saved estimate is not a substitute for the employer's approved register. The employer payroll guide explains the wider monthly process.

Keep a controlled employee file

Maintain the employment terms, pay changes, start and leaving dates, relevant employee identifiers and approved payment details. Keep evidence supporting tax reliefs, deductions or exemptions, including the period each document covers. Separate access to sensitive supporting documents from the wider payroll summary.

A pay-rise letter should connect to its effective date and the first payroll using it. If it is backdated, retain the calculation of the arrears instead of leaving an unexplained extra amount in the register.

Build a complete monthly payroll pack

RecordWhat it establishes
Approved earnings and attendance inputsWhy salary, overtime or leave adjustments were included.
Payroll register and calculation settingsHow gross pay became taxable pay and net pay.
Individual payslips and payment confirmationWhat was explained to the employee and what was paid.
Submitted returns and acknowledgementsWhat was reported for each obligation and period.
Payment references and receiptsWhat was remitted; match it to the relevant account.
Reconciliation and approvalWho checked totals and how differences were resolved.

NSSF's employer service provides separate return-management and electronic-payment functions. KRA similarly distinguishes a PAYE return from payment. Preserve both sides of the process rather than treating a successful submission as proof of settlement.

Use a reconciliation that someone else can follow

Suppose a payroll pack contains KES 300,000 gross cash earnings, KES 80,000 employee deductions and KES 220,000 net bank payments. The first control is that deductions plus net payments equal gross earnings. Employer-funded contributions sit outside that employee-deduction total.

Next, match the KES 80,000 deduction total to its separate destinations: tax, statutory contributions and other deductions. These illustrative totals do not prescribe tax rates. Investigate a difference rather than inserting a balancing number with no explanation.

Check retention requirements before deleting anything

KRA describes a requirement to retain tax records for at least five years. Treat that as a minimum tax-record reference, not permission to destroy every employment document on its fifth anniversary. Different records can have different retention triggers, and an unresolved assessment, dispute or other legal requirement may require preservation for longer.

Maintain a documented retention schedule identifying the record category, relevant legal basis, date from which the period runs and any hold preventing deletion. Keep backups readable and test restoration. When changing payroll providers, export the historical calculations and supporting records before access ends.

Preserve the correction trail and year-end totals

Keep the original result, reason for the change, approval and revised output. Link any amended return or additional payment to the correction. Reconcile annual employee tax records to the monthly payroll, including joiners, leavers and arrears.

For the submission evidence, use the PAYE return checklist. For the calculation trail, see salary arrears and PAYE and the payroll correction guide. A clear history protects both the employer and the employee from having to reconstruct decisions from memory.

title: Is Notice Pay Taxable in Kenya?
metaTitle: Is Notice Pay Taxable in Kenya? | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Understand PAYE on payment in lieu of notice, the period it relates to and the documents to check before accepting a Kenyan final settlement.
content:
Yes. Payment in lieu of notice is normally taxable employment income in Kenya. Being paid after your last working day does not by itself make it tax-free. The important checks are what the payment replaces, the period used for tax and whether the final statement separates it from salary, leave and other exit payments.

Use the Kenya PAYE calculator to understand ordinary salary deductions. It is not a terminal-settlement calculator: a payment allocated across periods needs a separate payroll calculation. The employment and tax guide explains the wider context.

Notice worked and notice paid are different records

If you work through a notice period, the salary for that work is recorded through payroll. Payment in lieu of notice replaces a period you do not work. Your employer should identify it as a separate item so its calculation can be checked against the contract or applicable employment terms.

Do not confuse notice pay with compensation for termination or a contractual gratuity. A settlement headed “terminal benefits” may contain all three, but that heading does not establish the tax treatment of each line. Start with the terminal-dues breakdown if the offer is presented as one total.

Which period does notice pay belong to?

KRA's lump-sum guidance places notice pay in the period immediately following termination. Ask payroll to show the dates covered, especially if a notice period runs across December and January. The transfer date alone does not explain the allocation.

The published examples in the older employer guide use historical tax bands. Copying their procedure is different from copying their rates. Ask which year's rules were applied and how income or tax already accounted for in the relevant period was treated.

A gross notice-pay example

Suppose the agreed notice entitlement is two months at KES 60,000 a month. The gross notice amount is KES 120,000. If the settlement also contains KES 18,000 unpaid salary and KES 12,000 unused leave, the gross settlement is KES 150,000, with three separately labelled lines.

These figures establish the gross entitlement only. They do not imply a fixed tax of 30% or a guaranteed net payment. The notice period, other income, applicable reliefs and the treatment of each component still matter. Keep the contractual salary basis explicit rather than assuming every allowance is included in the notice calculation.

What to ask payroll before payment

  • How many days or months of notice are being paid, and under which terms?
  • What salary basis and effective dates produce the gross amount?
  • Which tax period receives each part of the notice payment?
  • What PAYE has already been credited in that calculation?
  • Which other deductions reduce the bank payment, and why?

Request the calculation in writing, together with the final payslip and relevant P9 records. If another employer starts paying you during the same period, use the changing-jobs PAYE checklist to keep both sets of records consistent.

If the notice amount is disputed

A disagreement about how much notice you are owed is separate from whether payroll calculated tax correctly. Identify the disputed gross entitlement first, then ask for a revised tax calculation if the amount changes. Retain the original and corrected statements; the PAYE correction guide explains how to organise that evidence.

title: Is Unused Leave Pay Taxable in Kenya?
metaTitle: Is Unused Leave Pay Taxable in Kenya? | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Check tax on unused leave paid in cash in Kenya, reconcile your leave balance and understand why the year the days relate to matters.
content:
Yes. Cash paid for unused leave is generally taxable employment income in Kenya. The fact that you earned the days earlier, or receive the money after leaving a job, does not automatically exempt the payment. First confirm the leave balance and gross value; then check the period used to calculate tax.

Use the Kenya PAYE calculator to understand ordinary salary deductions. It is not a terminal-settlement calculator: a payment allocated across periods needs a separate payroll calculation. The employment and tax guide explains the wider context.

Start with the leave balance, not the tax percentage

Ask for a statement showing opening days, days earned, leave taken, approved adjustments and the closing balance being paid. Reconcile it to leave approvals and your employment terms. A payroll figure cannot establish whether an omitted day should have been paid.

Keep leave taken on full salary separate from a cash payment replacing untaken leave. Also distinguish annual leave from other absence categories; do not assume every recorded absence produces an encashment entitlement. This article explains tax on a payment that is due, rather than promising a universal right to cash out leave while still employed.

Match the payment to the year of the leave

KRA's lump-sum guidance says leave pay belongs to the year to which it relates. A schedule by year therefore matters when a final balance includes carried-forward days.

For example, a payment made in 2026 may include days attributable to 2025 and 2026. Ask payroll for that split and the supporting tax workings. Do not put the entire amount into an ordinary monthly calculator and assume its result settles the historical calculation. See salary arrears and PAYE for a related timing issue.

Worked example: check days and gross value

Assume the employer confirms 12 payable days and a documented daily rate of KES 2,000. The gross leave payment is 12 × KES 2,000 = KES 24,000. If five days relate to one year and seven to the next, the corresponding gross amounts are KES 10,000 and KES 14,000.

The daily rate here is an illustration, not a rule that all employers must divide salary by 30 or 26. Ask which pay elements and divisor were used under the applicable terms. A disagreement about the rate changes the gross payment before tax is considered.

Check the additional tax, not just the withholding line

The employer's calculation should identify the relevant income, rates, reliefs and tax already accounted for. The older KRA guide describes recalculating the relevant year's liability with an allocated lump sum and crediting tax already paid. That helps explain why a percentage shown against a final payment is not necessarily a special “leave tax” rate.

Do not automatically apply today's relief or contribution settings to earlier years. Ask payroll to explain any NSSF, health contribution, Housing Levy or other deduction separately; being taxable for PAYE does not establish every other deduction's basis.

Keep a trail if the balance changes

  1. Save the leave statement and gross calculation.
  2. Obtain the final payslip and payment confirmation.
  3. Check the year-by-year tax schedule against your P9 records.
  4. Request corrected records if days, salary basis or tax change.

The payslip guide helps separate gross pay from deductions. If the exit package includes more than leave, use the terminal-dues guide to keep the components distinct.

title: Redundancy Pay and Tax in Kenya
metaTitle: Redundancy Pay and Tax in Kenya | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Separate severance, notice, unused leave and gratuity in a Kenyan redundancy package, with a gross-payment example and practical PAYE checks.
content:
A redundancy package in Kenya is not automatically tax-free and should not be treated as one undifferentiated payment. Separate severance, notice, unused leave, outstanding salary and any contractual gratuity before checking PAYE. The entitlement calculation and the tax calculation answer different questions.

Use the Kenya PAYE calculator to understand ordinary salary deductions. It is not a terminal-settlement calculator: a payment allocated across periods needs a separate payroll calculation. The employment and tax guide explains the wider context.

Identify the gross entitlements first

Section 40 of the Employment Act includes payment for due leave, notice or wages in lieu, and severance of at least 15 days' pay for each completed year of service. Kenya Law's published judgment quoting section 40 sets out those conditions. Redundancy also has procedural requirements; paying a sum does not by itself establish that the process was lawful.

Check the employment contract and any applicable collective agreement for better terms. Ask for the completed service years, salary basis and daily-rate method. A disputed termination process or disputed entitlement may need employment advice independently of the tax review.

Example: build an itemised settlement

Assume an agreed calculation uses four completed years, 15 days per year and a daily pay basis of KES 2,000. The illustrated severance is 4 × 15 × KES 2,000 = KES 120,000. Suppose the approved statement also lists KES 60,000 notice pay, KES 20,000 leave pay and KES 10,000 salary outstanding.

ComponentGross amount
SeveranceKES 120,000
NoticeKES 60,000
Unused leaveKES 20,000
Outstanding salaryKES 10,000
TotalKES 210,000

This is an entitlement illustration using an assumed approved daily rate, not a universal salary divisor or a net-pay quote. The bank payment follows only after the treatment of each component and any other lawful deductions has been established.

Do not relabel severance as exempt gratuity

KRA's current Finance Act 2026 summary describes conditions for gratuity exemption: a service contract of at least three continuous years or the relevant extension, and gratuity no more than 31% of emoluments over the period. Those conditions do not establish that every redundancy payment is gratuity.

Ask payroll to identify the actual payment category and legal basis for any exemption. A pension-scheme benefit also needs its own analysis. The terminal-dues guide explains why these categories should remain separate.

Check allocation and tax already paid

KRA's lump-sum guidance treats taxable termination payments according to their nature and relevant periods. It distinguishes notice, leave and compensation under different contract arrangements. Ask for an allocation schedule rather than assuming every component is taxed in the transfer month or spread identically.

Have payroll show the applicable rates, reliefs, prior tax credits and any exemption separately. Historical KRA examples are useful for method, but their old rates are not current rates. Keep the payroll evidence checklist alongside the settlement.

Before agreeing the final figures

  • Reconcile service dates, salary basis and leave days.
  • Separate every gross payment and identify any disputed item.
  • Request the tax schedule and explanation of non-tax deductions.
  • Match the approved net amount to the payment received.
  • Keep the agreement, payslip, P9 and any corrected records.

If the tax calculation does not reconcile, follow the PAYE correction steps. Avoid accepting an unexplained percentage merely because the total is described as a redundancy package.

title: How Much of a Pay Rise Do You Keep?
metaTitle: How Much of a Pay Rise Do You Keep? | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: See the net value of a Kenyan salary increase, with worked examples below and above the NSSF ceiling and checks for your first revised payslip.
content:
A KES 10,000 pay rise does not mean KES 10,000 more in your bank account. To find the usable increase, calculate your old and new net salaries using the same assumptions, then subtract. The answer depends on your salary level, contribution limits and personal tax position.

Use the Kenya pay rise calculator for the comparison. The salary breakdown guide explains the deductions behind each result.

Compare two complete payslips

Work out gross salary, employee contributions, taxable income, PAYE and net pay twice. Do not subtract your current average deduction percentage from the proposed rise: the extra income can face a different marginal rate, while some contributions stop increasing at a ceiling.

Salary examples assume a resident employee with one job, a full month of regular cash salary, pensionable pay equal to gross pay, standard personal relief and February 2026 NSSF limits. They exclude extra pension, mortgage deductions, insurance relief, disability exemption, taxable benefits and personal repayments. Payroll rounding may differ slightly.

Example: KES 100,000 rising to KES 110,000

Monthly itemBeforeAfter
Gross salaryKES 100,000KES 110,000
Employee NSSFKES 6,000KES 6,480
SHIFKES 2,750KES 3,025
Housing LevyKES 1,500KES 1,650
PAYEKES 19,308.35KES 22,036.85
Net salaryKES 70,441.65KES 76,808.15

The extra cash is KES 6,366.50 a month: 63.665% of the KES 10,000 gross increase. Over 12 full months at unchanged rules and circumstances, that is KES 76,398. A rise starting part-way through the year does not produce 12 months of extra cash immediately.

Why the NSSF ceiling changes the result

NSSF's Year 4 notice sets the upper earnings limit at KES 108,000. In the example, only the first KES 8,000 of the increase adds employee NSSF. A rise entirely above that ceiling adds no further mandatory employee NSSF under these assumptions.

For example, KES 120,000 rising to KES 130,000 gives net pay of KES 83,510.65 and KES 90,213.15: a KES 6,702.50 increase. This differs from the first example even though both gross increases are KES 10,000. See the NSSF contribution guide for the tiers.

A higher tax band does not re-tax all your salary

Kenya uses progressive bands. If an increase crosses a band boundary, only the relevant portion enters the higher band; the entire salary does not suddenly face that rate. Qualifying deductions also affect taxable pay before PAYE is calculated.

Keep three percentages separate: the gross percentage rise, the net percentage rise, and the share of extra gross cash retained. They have different denominators. There is no universal rule that the percentage increase in net salary must always be lower than the percentage increase in gross salary.

Check the first revised payslip

  • Confirm the effective date and whether the rise includes existing allowances.
  • Separate recurring salary from a one-off payment.
  • Check personal deductions or benefit changes separately.
  • Reconcile the new net figure with the bank deposit.

A backdated increase needs the salary arrears checklist. If the employer quotes a package instead of cash salary, first use the gross versus net salary guide.

For the supporting records, follow our salary review letters: what to check checklist.

title: Salary vs Benefits: Comparing Job Offers
metaTitle: Salary vs Benefits: Comparing Job Offers | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Compare cash salary with medical cover, pension, cars and other benefits in Kenya without confusing employer cost, taxable value and personal value.
content:
A benefits package can be valuable without increasing the money available for rent or groceries. When comparing salary with benefits in Kenya, keep three figures separate: cash received, the tax cost of a benefit and the expense that benefit genuinely saves you.

Start with the salary comparison calculator for the cash salaries. Then use the salary breakdown guide and the benefit details to build a personal comparison.

Sort the offer into four categories

CategoryWhat to check
Regular cashBasic pay and allowances already included in gross salary.
Non-cash benefitsWhat you receive, its payroll tax valuation and any employee charge.
Deferred benefitsPension contributions, access conditions and any vesting rules.
Conditional paymentsBonus criteria, approval and whether the amount is guaranteed.

Do not add a house or commuter allowance twice if it already forms part of the quoted gross. The cash allowances guide explains why the label alone does not make cash tax-free.

Employer cost is not your personal value

An employer might describe a benefit as costing KES 8,000 per month. That does not mean it adds KES 8,000 to your bank balance, saves you that amount, or has that taxable value. Ask for all three figures separately.

For medical cover, compare the actual cover schedule: eligible dependants, provider network, limits, exclusions and any employee premium. KRA lists employer medical cover among employment income not chargeable to PAYE; a cash medical allowance is a different arrangement. Ask payroll which treatment applies to the exact offer.

Allow for tax on non-cash benefits

A taxable car or housing benefit can increase the PAYE bill without increasing cash earnings. Ask the employer for the payroll valuation rather than entering the vehicle's purchase price or the employer's full cost as monthly income. Our benefits-in-kind guide covers that distinction.

As a narrow illustration, if an additional KES 10,000 of taxable benefit falls wholly within a 30% band and nothing else changes, the extra PAYE is KES 3,000. The benefit has not paid you KES 10,000 cash; you must assess its usefulness against the KES 3,000 tax cost and any employee charge. This is not a valuation formula for a car or home.

Value savings you will actually make

Suppose package A provides KES 75,000 net cash and cover that would replace KES 4,000 of your own monthly spending. Package B provides KES 78,000 net cash without that cover. On those assumed facts, A offers KES 79,000 of cash plus avoided expenditure versus B's KES 78,000, but only KES 75,000 is spendable salary.

These are decision examples, not calculated payroll quotations. If you would not buy equivalent cover, or the policies differ materially, the assumed KES 4,000 saving needs revising. Do not count the same avoided expense again in your monthly budget.

Keep retirement savings and bonuses separate

Employer pension funding may improve long-term value but cannot automatically pay today's bills. Check the scheme terms and employee contribution required. Keep a discretionary bonus outside the guaranteed monthly budget, then model it as a separate upside scenario.

Before accepting, obtain a written package breakdown and sample payroll calculation. Use the pension saving trade-offs to judge liquidity, and compare the full offers using the two-offer worksheet.

For an exchange within your current job, check the salary sacrifice proposal before changing payroll.
