title: How to Compare Two Salary Offers
metaTitle: How to Compare Two Salary Offers | PAYE Calculator
metaDescription: Compare Kenyan job offers using net pay, commuting costs, guaranteed annual income and first-year cash flow, with a practical worked comparison.
content:
Compare two salary offers by putting them on the same basis: guaranteed cash, estimated deductions, unavoidable job costs and the period covered. A higher headline salary can leave less usable money if commuting or other required costs rise sharply.

Use the Kenya salary comparison calculator for the payroll starting point. The salary breakdown guide helps identify which figures belong in the comparison.

Build one worksheet with matching columns

For each job, record regular gross cash salary, estimated net salary, required employee contributions, commuting costs and any other unavoidable work expense. List benefits alongside those cash figures rather than treating them as salary. Record the source of each assumption: offer letter, payroll illustration or your own expense estimate.

Check whether an annual package includes employer pension funding or statutory employer costs. Dividing such a package by 12 may not give monthly gross cash pay. The gross and net salary explainer provides the terminology to use when asking HR.

Example: higher salary, higher travel costs

Salary examples assume a resident employee with one job, a full month of regular cash salary, pensionable pay equal to gross pay, standard personal relief and February 2026 NSSF limits. They exclude extra pension, mortgage deductions, insurance relief, disability exemption, taxable benefits and personal repayments. Payroll rounding may differ slightly.

Monthly comparisonOffer AOffer B
Gross cash salaryKES 100,000KES 110,000
Estimated net salaryKES 70,441.65KES 76,808.15
Assumed commuting costKES 4,000KES 9,000
Cash after commutingKES 66,441.65KES 67,808.15

Offer B pays KES 6,366.50 more net, but leaves only KES 1,366.50 more after these illustrative travel costs. The expense figures are assumptions, not Nairobi market averages. Replace them with your actual route, working days and fares or vehicle costs.

Annualise only the guaranteed parts

Multiply regular monthly figures by the number of months you will actually receive them. Keep a guaranteed contractual payment separate from a discretionary target bonus. For a full unchanged 12-month period, the example's after-commuting difference is KES 16,398.

Then create a first-year cash-flow view. A later start date, unpaid gap between jobs, relocation payment, deposit or one-off joining expense can change the first-year result without changing the recurring monthly comparison. Do not quietly mix first-year costs into a permanent annual figure.

Compare benefits and working conditions beside cash

Record medical cover, employer pension, leave, working hours, location requirements and the stability of any flexible-working agreement. Use the salary versus benefits guide to value the costs a benefit replaces without pretending every benefit is cash.

Decide which non-cash conditions are essential before scoring the offers. A longer commute or unpredictable working hours may matter more to you than the last few thousand shillings. There is no universal weighting that makes one package objectively best for every household.

Test the uncertain assumptions

  • Run the comparison with no discretionary bonus.
  • Increase the estimated travel cost to a plausible high-cost month.
  • Check whether personal deductions or reliefs differ between the payroll illustrations.
  • Ask when salary reviews and benefits begin, including any probation conditions.
  • Request written confirmation of any change negotiated verbally.

Finally, save the offer and calculation assumptions. When moving jobs, follow the PAYE records checklist for changing employers so the first payslip can be reconciled to what you accepted.

title: How to Correct a PAYE Return on iTax
metaTitle: How to Correct a PAYE Return on iTax | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Correct an employer PAYE return on iTax, reconcile the change with payments and P9 records, and understand approval for a reduced liability.
content:
To correct a filed Kenyan PAYE return, use iTax’s amended-return process for the affected employer obligation and period. First establish what is wrong: a payroll calculation, the information filed, or the allocation of a payment. These are different problems and may need different remedies.

Use the employer cost calculator to cross-check ordinary payroll costs, then the employer payroll guide for the wider monthly process. A calculator does not amend a return or determine the treatment of historical payments.

Build a correction pack before logging in

Collect the original return and acknowledgement, payroll register, payment references, receipts and the documents supporting the change. Make a short schedule showing each affected employee, original figure, corrected figure and reason. Keep the employer PIN, tax obligation and return month visible on the cover sheet.

If only the payment was posted to the wrong period, do not change accurate salary figures to make the ledger balance. Ask KRA to resolve the payment allocation. If the underlying payslip is wrong, start with the PAYE calculation correction checklist.

Use the amended-return route

  1. Sign in through the official iTax portal using the employer’s authorised access.
  2. Under Returns, choose File Amended Return. Confirm Income Tax – PAYE and the affected period.
  3. Use the current official form and instructions for that period. Reconcile the complete revised return, not just the difference you want to change.
  4. Validate the file and resolve errors against the supporting payroll records before submitting.
  5. Save the submission acknowledgement and monitor the amendment status and resulting ledger entries.

KRA’s correction FAQ identifies the amended-return option. Interface fields and templates can change; follow the current portal prompts rather than an old screenshot. Retain both versions, with an explanation of who reviewed the correction.

An increase and a decrease are handled differently

KRA’s amendment guidance says an increase in liability is automatically validated, while a decrease is subject to approval before it reflects in iTax. Submission alone therefore does not prove a reduced balance has been accepted.

Do not assume an approved reduction automatically becomes a cash refund, or deduct it from a later payment without checking the account and applicable procedure. Keep any KRA requests and responses with the correction pack.

Example: reconcile liability and money already paid

Suppose the original return declared KES 40,000 PAYE, but the supported corrected total is KES 45,000. The increase is KES 5,000. If KES 40,000 has already been correctly allocated, that leaves KES 5,000 principal before any applicable penalties or interest. If nothing was paid, the outstanding principal is not just the KES 5,000 difference.

Conversely, a correction from KES 40,000 to KES 35,000 requests a KES 5,000 reduction. Track approval and the ledger outcome. These are reconciliation examples, not tax-rate calculations.

Close the employee and employer records together

Update affected payroll summaries and P9 records so they can be reconciled to accepted returns. Tell the employee what changed and which period it affects; do not quietly overwrite the old evidence. For the normal monthly process, see filing PAYE returns. Use the payroll records checklist to retain the complete trail.

title: Nil PAYE Returns in Kenya Explained
metaTitle: Nil PAYE Returns in Kenya Explained | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Know when a Kenyan employer needs a nil PAYE return, check the filing period and distinguish zero tax from cancelled obligations or unpaid payroll.
content:
A nil PAYE return tells KRA that there is no PAYE to declare for the relevant period. It is not a request to postpone payment, and it does not close the employer’s PAYE registration. KRA expressly requires a nil return when there is no PAYE to declare.

Before deciding that a month is nil, reconcile the payroll. The employer cost calculator helps distinguish employee deductions from employer costs; the employer guide puts the return alongside the other monthly obligations.

Check why the month appears to be nil

SituationWhat to check
No employees or employment payments in the periodConfirm there are no final payments, arrears or taxable benefits overlooked.
Payroll calculation produces zero PAYERetain the calculation and check the current return’s employee and other reporting requirements.
PAYE was deducted but the business cannot payThis is a liability, not a nil month.
The business has stopped tradingCheck the obligation’s formal status; inactivity does not itself cancel registration.

A zero bank payment does not by itself establish zero taxable employment income. Benefits, deductions, salary timing and final settlements can complicate the picture. Resolve those items before making the declaration.

File for the correct employer and period

  1. Confirm the employer PIN and active PAYE obligation.
  2. Review the month’s payroll and supporting records, including payments to former staff.
  3. Sign in at the official iTax portal and use the appropriate nil-return route for Income Tax – PAYE.
  4. Check the period and declaration carefully before submitting.
  5. Download the acknowledgement and verify the period appears as filed.

The official PAYE return guide shows a File Nil Return option. If the portal asks for other payroll or levy information, follow those current instructions; do not erase real employee information merely to force a zero return. Keep the evidence explaining why PAYE was nil with the acknowledgement.

The deadline still applies

KRA states that the monthly PAYE return is due by the ninth day of the following month. For example, an October return is due by 9 November. A month with no PAYE to declare should not simply be skipped.

KRA lists the late-filing penalty as the higher of 25% of tax due and KES 10,000. Zero tax therefore does not mean there is no late-filing exposure. Check any actual assessment with KRA rather than assuming a nil return removes an existing penalty.

Nil PAYE does not settle other obligations

Check NSSF, SHA/SHIF, Housing Levy and any other applicable employer obligations separately. Their bases and filing or payment requirements are not established by the PAYE total. The payroll setup checklist helps identify the accounts that need a separate reconciliation.

Likewise, the employer’s monthly PAYE return is different from an employee’s individual income tax return. Do not choose an individual nil income-tax declaration when the task is an employer PAYE return.

If staff have left or the business has closed

KRA allows an application to cancel a tax obligation through iTax. Its cancellation guidance says to continue filing and paying as required until official confirmation of cancellation arrives. Save that confirmation and its effective date; an application receipt is not the same thing.

If a nil return was filed but taxable payroll is later identified, investigate a PAYE return amendment. For a month with PAYE to report, follow the normal PAYE filing process.

title: Employee Exit Payroll Checklist: Kenya
metaTitle: Employee Exit Payroll Checklist: Kenya | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Close a Kenyan employee’s payroll accurately: confirm dates, itemise final pay, reconcile deductions, provide tax records and track later adjustments.
content:
An employee exit is not complete when a name disappears from next month’s payroll. The employer still needs an agreed calculation, payment evidence, statutory reconciliation and a usable record of pay and tax. Use this checklist to assign each step and avoid leaving a final settlement in an email chain.

The employer cost calculator can cross-check ordinary salary costs. It is not a terminal-dues calculator: notice, leave, severance and gratuity require separate classification. Use the employer payroll guide for the wider controls.

1. Confirm dates and outstanding inputs

Record the last day worked, contractual cessation date, period covered by salary and planned payment date. These may differ. Ask the responsible manager to approve attendance, overtime, commission and leave records before payroll closes.

Check the contract and exit documents for notice arrangements and any agreed payments. Do not assume that resignation, expiry of a fixed-term contract and redundancy create identical entitlements. Route a disputed entitlement for resolution rather than choosing a convenient payroll label.

2. Build an itemised final-pay schedule

  • Salary earned and any unpaid earlier salary.
  • Approved overtime, commission or bonus.
  • Unused leave paid in cash, with days and the rate used.
  • Notice worked or payment in lieu of notice.
  • Any severance, gratuity or other separately identified payment.
  • Reimbursements and each proposed deduction, supported individually.

For example, an approved schedule might contain KES 30,000 salary, KES 12,000 leave pay and KES 40,000 notice pay: KES 82,000 gross before deductions. That addition does not establish the tax due or whether each amount is legally payable. Keep the assumptions beside the figures.

Read unused leave pay and tax and notice pay and PAYE before combining those lines. Do not treat the whole settlement as an ordinary monthly salary or automatically exempt income.

3. Reconcile tax and deductions before payment

Document the period to which each taxable component relates, the applicable treatment and tax already accounted for. Review every non-tax deduction against its supporting records and lawful basis. An equipment handover issue is not, by itself, a calculation of an amount deductible from wages.

Have a second reviewer compare the approved gross components, deductions and net amount. Separately identify employer-funded costs so they are not accidentally charged to the employee. Give the employee an understandable breakdown and a contact for specific discrepancies.

4. Prepare the employee’s pay and tax records

KRA describes the P9 as the employer-issued summary of employment income for the year. As an exit control, reconcile the employee’s pay and tax record through the final payment and give them a clear statement of the figures. Agree how they will receive the year-end P9 after their work email closes; a bank receipt alone cannot explain the tax history.

For the employee’s next payroll, see changing jobs and PAYE records. Keep the tax certificate distinct from other employment documents.

5. Close remittances and leave a controlled adjustment route

Match deductions to the relevant submissions and payments, then retain acknowledgements and receipts. Removing a person from future regular salary runs should not delete their history or hide an unpaid deduction. Use the payroll records checklist for the archive.

Assign someone to handle a later bonus, arrears payment or correction. Recheck its tax treatment and update affected records rather than reopening the employee as an ordinary full-month starter. Maintain a closing log with the final payment date, outstanding items, owner and resolution evidence. That makes the exit auditable even after the original payroll administrator has moved on.

For the related practical checks, read Pension Transfers When Changing Jobs.

For the supporting records, follow our how to check a certificate of service in kenya checklist.

Before agreeing a recovery, use the detailed payroll loan balance checklist.

title: NSSF Tier II Contracting Out: Employer Checklist
metaTitle: NSSF Tier II Contracting Out: Employer Checklist | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Understand RBA approval for NSSF Tier II contracting out, separate scheme qualification from employer approval and reconcile contributions after a change.
content:
NSSF Tier II contracting out allows an approved employer arrangement to direct Tier II contributions to a qualifying retirement scheme. It is not permission to stop pension deductions or replace them with an ordinary savings account. Before changing payroll, establish the approval, scheme and effective period.

Use the NSSF calculator to split the contribution. The statutory deductions guide explains how this fits alongside the rest of payroll. This checklist concerns implementing an arrangement, rather than choosing an investment provider.

Separate the two approval questions

The Retirement Benefits Authority notice identifies an employer application using Form C1 and its required attachments. Separately, the receiving scheme must satisfy the Reference Scheme Test and receive the relevant certificate. Evidence that a scheme qualifies does not, by itself, establish that your employer’s arrangement has been approved.

Obtain the current form and regulations from RBA’s NSSF downloads. Have the scheme administrator help assemble the required attachments. Do not rely on a provider’s marketing page as the approval document or assume every existing occupational pension automatically qualifies.

Build a controlled changeover file

  • Identify the legal employer, proposed receiving scheme and responsible administrator.
  • Retain the submitted application, attachments, correspondence and approval.
  • Confirm which employees and contribution periods the arrangement covers.
  • Record the agreed remittance details and reporting process using verified channels.
  • Assign a payroll reviewer to approve the first split and reconcile both destinations.

These are practical implementation controls, not a substitute for the official application requirements. If the start date or scope is unclear, resolve it with RBA and the administrator before redirecting contributions. Keep a separate list of any earlier months needing correction; changing next month’s destination does not explain a historical gap.

Example: split the amount, not the employee’s entitlement

Under the February 2026 limits, pensionable pay of KES 50,000 gives KES 540 employee Tier I and KES 2,460 employee Tier II. The employer matches each amount. The combined Tier I amount is therefore KES 1,080 and Tier II is KES 4,920, totalling KES 6,000.

Where the approved arrangement applies, reconcile Tier I with NSSF and Tier II with the approved scheme. Do not deduct the employer’s KES 3,000 share from the employee, or add the statutory Tier II amount twice because the scheme has a separate payroll code. Any additional occupational pension contribution needs its own clear description.

The NSSF rates guide covers the bands and other salary examples. Use the period’s limits rather than copying the current ceiling into older payroll.

Explain the change to employees

Give employees the scheme name, how to obtain statements and the first affected month. Show the employee contribution separately from the employer match. Explain which record should show each tier so that a legitimate split is not mistaken for missing money.

After the first remittance, match payroll totals to payment evidence and individual allocations at both destinations. A bulk receipt is only part of that reconciliation. For checking the NSSF side, use the contribution-statement guide; for unresolved differences, follow the missing-contributions checklist.

title: HELB Deductions Not Remitted: What Next?
metaTitle: HELB Deductions Not Remitted: What Next? | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Trace HELB deductions missing from your loan statement, request employer remittance evidence and escalate unresolved credits through official channels.
content:
If HELB appears on your payslip but the payment is missing from your loan statement, start a documented reconciliation with payroll and HELB. A payslip proves that payroll recorded a deduction; it does not establish that the money reached the correct loan account.

Use the PAYE and net salary calculator to separate tax from the cash effect of loan repayments, and the employment situations guide for related payroll questions. The task here is tracing a missing credit, not recalculating the loan’s interest or assuming the debt has disappeared.

1. Match the month before reporting a gap

Download a dated statement through HELB’s official borrower services. Compare the payroll month, deduction amount and any later credit. HELB’s employer guidance requires deductions to be remitted by the fifteenth day of the following month, so distinguish a not-yet-due remittance from an older unexplained omission.

For example, if September and October payslips each show KES 5,000 but the statement contains only one matching KES 5,000 credit, identify which month that credit covers. The unreconciled deduction is KES 5,000, not automatically a new fee or proof that both months were unpaid. Ask for allocation details where the statement description is unclear.

2. Request evidence for your own deduction

Send payroll the affected months and amounts. Ask for the remittance date, receipt or transaction reference, confirmation of the borrower identifier used and confirmation that you were included in the submitted schedule. Request only your relevant entry, with colleagues’ personal details removed.

HELB’s published employer payment workflow separates uploading the remittance list from completing payment and obtaining a receipt. A prepared list or payment request is not the same as a completed remittance. An employer’s aggregate receipt also needs to be matched to your individual allocation.

Please help trace my HELB deduction of KES [amount] for [month]. It appears on my payslip but I cannot match it to my statement dated [date]. Please confirm the identifier, remittance reference, payment date and my entry in the schedule, or explain the correction needed.

3. Escalate an unresolved credit to HELB

Gather the payslips, dated loan statement, employer details, available references and your payroll correspondence. Use the official HELB contacts to ask whether the payment is unreceived, unallocated or linked to incorrect details. Request an enquiry reference and record the advice and next action.

HELB’s borrower FAQ states that unremitted employer deductions attract an employer penalty of 5% per month. That does not mean a disputed credit will appear automatically, or that you should stop monitoring repayment. Ask HELB how to handle any loan-account consequences while the employer remittance is investigated; do not invent an adjustment in your own records.

4. Verify the correction before closing the query

Obtain an updated statement after payment or reallocation is confirmed. Check each disputed amount rather than just whether the balance fell: other payments or charges may also have changed it. Keep the original statement and the written explanation of the correction.

Before paying again to cover the same disputed deduction, ask HELB how the original amount will be traced and how a duplicate would be treated. Use verified official payment instructions; never send passwords or one-time codes to someone offering to fix the record.

For routine deduction amounts, read how HELB payroll repayments work. If you have left the employer, retain the same evidence alongside your exit payroll records. A job change does not resolve an earlier missing remittance.

title: Can Your Employer Deduct Your Salary?
metaTitle: Can Your Employer Deduct Your Salary? | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check the basis for a Kenyan salary deduction, understand the general deduction limit and prepare a clear payroll query with supporting evidence.
content:
A Kenyan employer can make certain deductions from wages, but a payroll label alone does not make a deduction lawful. Check three things separately: the legal basis, the amount and whether money intended for another organisation was actually remitted.

Use the PAYE and net salary calculator for an estimate of ordinary statutory deductions. It cannot decide whether a disputed damage charge, loan recovery or absence deduction is lawful. The employment situations guide provides related payroll explanations.

Start with the reason for the deduction

Section 19 of the Employment Act lists permitted categories with conditions. These include deductions authorised by law or specified instruments, erroneous wage overpayments, qualifying written requests and repayments of employer loans under written agreements. Damage deductions concern wilful default; they are not a blanket permission to charge staff for every accident.

Ask payroll to identify the relevant category and supporting evidence. If the explanation is “company policy”, ask how that policy and the particular charge meet the applicable requirements. Do not assume signing a general handbook authorises every future deduction.

Check the amount separately from the authority

Section 19 sets a general ceiling of two-thirds of wages for the deductions under that section, subject to any prescribed different amount. For employer loans under a written agreement, the repayment deduction cannot exceed 50% of wages remaining after the other section 19 deductions. A deduction below the overall ceiling still needs a lawful basis.

For a simple illustration, if the applicable wages are KES 60,000, two-thirds is KES 40,000, leaving KES 20,000. This is arithmetic, not an assessment of a particular payslip: confirm the relevant wage figure, deduction categories and any applicable exception. Do not treat KES 40,000 as a free allowance for the employer to invent charges.

Separate a wage deduction from a change in pay

A line subtracting money from earned wages is different from a proposed change to contractual salary, or a disagreement about how much salary was earned. Ask which situation applies before comparing figures. Record the period and effective date rather than arguing only about the final bank transfer.

For an absence adjustment, gather attendance records, leave approval and the calculation used. For an alleged overpayment, request a comparison between what should have been paid and what was actually paid. For damage, ask for the incident details, evidence and valuation. These records help test the explanation; they do not establish liability by themselves.

Build a one-page deduction query

  • Name the payroll month and exact deduction label.
  • State the amount and why you cannot reconcile it.
  • Ask for the basis, calculation and relevant agreement or instruction.
  • Attach only the documents needed for the issue.
  • Request a written response and retain the correction trail.

A useful opening is: “My [month] payslip includes KES [amount] for [label]. Please provide the basis and calculation, including the period covered, and explain how this complies with the applicable deduction limits.”

Use the payslip reading guide to distinguish employee deductions from employer contributions shown for information. If the disputed line is income tax, use the wrong PAYE checklist instead of treating all deductions as discretionary charges.

Follow up unresolved deductions

Keep the contract, payslips, bank records and responses together. If payroll cannot resolve the issue, consider your union representative, a labour officer or a qualified employment adviser. Ask what route and time limits apply to your circumstances rather than assuming every wage complaint follows the same process.

Where the money was meant for a third party, check its receipt separately. For example, missing HELB remittances require loan-statement reconciliation as well as an explanation from payroll. A corrected payslip is not proof that the intended recipient has been paid.

title: PAYE on a Partial Month of Salary
metaTitle: PAYE on a Partial Month of Salary | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check Kenyan PAYE when you start or leave mid-month: establish actual earnings, calculate taxable pay and avoid simply dividing a full-month tax figure.
content:
When you work only part of a month, first establish the pay earned for that period, then calculate PAYE on the resulting taxable pay. Dividing a normal month’s PAYE by the fraction of days worked can give the wrong answer because tax bands and relief affect the calculation.

Use the PAYE calculator with the actual gross earnings for the period, after confirming which deductions and benefits apply. The employment situations guide covers related changes at work.

Agree the earnings before calculating tax

Ask payroll for the start or leaving date, the pay period and the basis used to calculate salary. A contractual monthly salary is not necessarily the amount earned in the first run. Calendar days, working days and a fixed divisor can produce different figures; do not assume one method applies to every employment arrangement.

For example, an agreed calculation might produce KES 30,000 gross from a normal KES 60,000 salary. That establishes earnings only. It does not establish KES 30,000 taxable pay, because allowable deductions or taxable benefits can change the tax base. Keep the approved calculation with the first payslip.

Calculate tax from taxable pay

KRA’s PAYE guidance sets out monthly bands and personal relief. For an isolated tax illustration, assume payroll has established KES 30,000 taxable pay, the employee qualifies for KES 2,400 personal relief, and there are no other reliefs or exemptions. Tax before relief is KES 2,400 on the first KES 24,000 plus KES 1,500 on the next KES 6,000. PAYE is therefore KES 1,500.

This is not a net-salary example: it starts after allowable deductions. It also assumes no overlapping employer or special residency issue. Compare it with KES 60,000 taxable pay under the same assumptions: PAYE is KES 10,383.35. Half of that, KES 5,191.68 rounded, is not the KES 1,500 result for KES 30,000 taxable pay. Progressive tax makes a simple proportional shortcut unreliable.

Review each deduction independently

Ask which earnings base and period payroll used for NSSF, SHIF and the Housing Levy. Do not halve every statutory amount merely because the salary is reduced, or treat every deduction from cash as tax-deductible. Use the taxable-pay explanation to follow the bridge from gross earnings to the tax base.

Check separately whether an allowance, benefit or reimbursement applies for the partial period. A full monthly benefit valuation or a payment for another period should not disappear just because basic salary is smaller. Ask for the reason for each entry rather than assuming it shares the same proration rule.

Check overlapping jobs and delayed first pay

If your old employer also pays you in the month, tell payroll and keep both payslips. Read PAYE when changing jobs before treating two calculations as an accurate annual result. If the first payment includes earnings from an earlier period, request an allocation rather than calling the entire amount ordinary pay for the payment month.

Send payroll a focused query

State the contractual salary, dates worked, gross amount used and the line you cannot reconcile. Ask for the taxable-pay calculation and relief applied. Resolve the earnings question first; a perfectly calculated tax amount can still be based on the wrong salary. Retain the response for your year-end P9 reconciliation.

For this specific situation, use our sick-pay entitlement and half-pay checks to check the supporting records and payroll calculation.

title: How to Check Your P9 Against Payslips
metaTitle: How to Check Your P9 Against Payslips | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Reconcile a Kenyan P9 month by month against payslips, benefits, deductions and PAYE before using the figures in your annual tax return.
content:
Check your P9 by matching each monthly entry to the corresponding payroll records, then adding the columns yourself. A matching annual total is useful, but it can hide an omitted month offset by a duplicated one.

The PAYE calculator helps investigate an ordinary monthly tax calculation. It does not verify tax credits or replace an employer-issued P9. Keep the salary breakdowns guide beside your records if gross, taxable and net pay are being confused.

Collect a complete set before comparing totals

Gather the P9 for the correct year, all available payslips, records of off-cycle payments and explanations of corrections. Check your name and KRA PIN, the employer identity and the employment months. If you worked for several employers, keep a separate reconciliation for each before combining the figures for filing.

KRA’s filing guidance says employment income from all employers belongs in one individual return. Do not discard a P9 merely because you left that employer early in the year. Nor should you insert twelve months of salary where you were employed for only part of the year.

Match like with like

The official KRA P9 template separates basic salary, non-cash benefits, housing value, deductions, chargeable pay, tax charged and reliefs. That means the bank deposit is not the number to compare with P9 gross pay. A taxable non-cash benefit can affect the tax record without adding cash to your account.

Create a worksheet with one row per month and columns for the P9 figure, supporting payroll figure, difference and explanation. Start with earnings, then allowable deductions, then tax and relief. Use the payslip reading guide to identify which entries are totals rather than extra deductions.

Use the differences to locate the problem

Suppose three payslips show PAYE of KES 8,000, KES 8,500 and KES 9,000. Their total is KES 25,500. If the corresponding P9 entries total KES 24,500, the KES 1,000 difference is a query to investigate, not proof of an automatic refund. Compare each month to find whether there is a transcription error, a correction or a payment not included in the documents.

Record rounding separately from unexplained differences. Do not change several figures merely to force the annual total to agree. For a reversed payment, request both the original and correcting record so the same income or tax is not counted twice.

Check reliefs and exceptional payments

Ask payroll to explain months with an unusual relief amount or deduction, using the evidence you supplied. Compare bonuses, arrears and terminal payments with their supporting schedules. Their tax allocation may require more explanation than a single bank-transfer date provides.

For a change of employer, use the changing-jobs reconciliation checklist. For a suspected calculation error, follow the wrong PAYE checklist rather than assuming every P9 mismatch has the same cause.

Resolve and retain the final version

Send payroll a short list of affected months and columns, attach the relevant evidence and request an explanation or corrected P9. Keep the original, corrected version and correspondence. Check any pre-populated filing figures against the resolved records; pre-population is not a reason to ignore a known mismatch.

KRA’s individual filing FAQs explain the employment-income return option where employer data is available and the route for amending an erroneous return. If the P9 is missing, request it and follow current official filing instructions. A self-created spreadsheet is a reconciliation aid, not an employer’s certification.

title: Salary Overpayments: Payroll Reconciliation
metaTitle: Salary Overpayments: Payroll Reconciliation | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Separate a duplicate bank transfer from a salary calculation error, reconcile gross and net differences and document payroll corrections in Kenya.
content:
A salary overpayment needs two reconciliations: what payroll should have calculated and what money actually moved. A duplicate bank transfer is different from entering the wrong salary in payroll. Establish which happened before agreeing a recovery figure.

Use the PAYE calculator to cross-check an ordinary salary calculation, and the employer payroll guide for the wider control process. The calculator cannot decide a disputed repayment obligation or correct filed tax records.

Identify the type of error

  • Payment error: payroll was correct, but the bank instruction paid the net salary twice or sent the wrong amount.
  • Earnings error: payroll used an incorrect salary, duplicated allowance or wrong number of days.
  • Deduction error: earnings were correct, but tax or another deduction was incorrectly calculated or omitted.

Ask for the approved pay terms, original payslip and payment references. Record the relevant month and whether a later adjustment has already been made. Otherwise an amount recovered once through payroll might accidentally be requested again by bank transfer.

Example: a duplicate transfer

Suppose a correct payslip shows KES 70,000 net, but two KES 70,000 transfers reach the employee. Total cash received is KES 140,000 and the payment difference is KES 70,000. That difference does not establish a second month of earned salary. Confirm the transaction evidence and payroll record before deciding what needs correction.

If payroll itself was also duplicated, the case is no longer only a bank-payment error. Ask whether the duplicate reached the payroll register, statutory schedules or tax return. A single repayment does not automatically repair those records.

Example: an incorrect gross salary

For illustration, suppose original payroll records show gross earnings of KES 100,000 and total employee deductions of KES 30,000, giving KES 70,000 net. A supported recalculation shows KES 90,000 gross, KES 27,000 deductions and KES 63,000 net. The gross difference is KES 10,000, the deduction difference KES 3,000 and the cash difference KES 7,000.

These invented figures illustrate reconciliation only; they are not Kenyan statutory deduction calculations. They show why demanding the gross difference without explaining tax and other deductions can leave the employee unable to reconcile the request. Obtain a written schedule explaining the proposed recovery and how each deduction adjustment will be handled.

Keep recovery and tax correction separate

Confirm the basis and applicable limits for any deduction from future wages. See salary deduction rules for that separate legal question. Do not assume a payroll error permits an unlimited deduction or that an informal repayment plan settles the tax treatment.

Where a filed return needs amendment, use the PAYE return correction process. KRA’s amendment guidance distinguishes automatic validation of increased liability from approval for a decrease. A submitted reduction is not evidence that a cash refund has been paid.

Close the case with a signed-off reconciliation

Retain the original and corrected payroll calculations, evidence of money returned or recovered, and the status of each tax or contribution correction. Identify who is responsible for each outstanding action. Verify repayment instructions through the employer’s normal finance channel before transferring money.

Ask for confirmation of the remaining balance after every instalment and check the next payslip for unintended duplicate recovery. Update the year-end P9 only through the employer’s controlled correction process; KRA’s tax deduction card records monthly income and tax figures that should remain explainable. Use the payroll records checklist to retain the audit trail. If the amount or entitlement remains disputed, obtain appropriate employment or tax advice before treating the case as resolved.

title: PAYE on Commission in Kenya
metaTitle: PAYE on Commission in Kenya | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check tax on employee sales commission in Kenya, reconcile the commission schedule and distinguish payroll PAYE from withholding on business payments.
content:
Commission earned as an employee is employment income for Kenyan PAYE. Start by checking the commission amount and the employment arrangement, then reconcile it to payroll. A payment labelled “commission” does not automatically belong under the withholding-tax treatment used for a separate business payment.

Use the PAYE calculator to compare ordinary salary with the approved commission-inclusive pay. The employment situations guide explains related payroll changes. This guide focuses on the sales schedule and classification questions that come before the tax calculation.

Confirm whether this is employee remuneration

KRA’s PAYE guidance expressly includes commissions among taxable cash employment payments. Ask whether the payment arises from your employment contract or a genuinely separate business arrangement. Being paid outside the normal salary transfer does not, by itself, change the nature of the income.

KRA also publishes withholding-tax guidance for specified payments. Do not borrow a withholding percentage from an agency invoice and apply it to your employee commission. If your arrangement is unclear, request a written explanation of the classification. See employment versus freelance income before comparing the two systems.

Reconcile the sales schedule first

Request the eligible sales, contractual rate, approval date and any exclusions or cancellations. Check whether the agreement uses invoiced sales, money collected or another measure. VAT, refunds and discounts should be handled according to the applicable arrangement, not guessed from the headline sales total.

For example, assume the approved commission base is KES 400,000 and the contractual rate is 3%. Gross commission is KES 12,000. If payroll shows KES 9,000, the unexplained difference is KES 3,000 before considering tax. Ask whether a sale was excluded or the schedule changed; do not assume that a lower gross entry is simply PAYE.

Compare the complete tax calculations

Once the gross amount is established, ask for ordinary taxable pay and revised taxable pay after the commission and applicable deductions. For a narrow illustration, if taxable pay rises from KES 60,000 to KES 72,000, and the entire extra KES 12,000 lies in the 30% band with relief unchanged, additional PAYE is KES 3,600.

This is a tax-only comparison, not a promise of KES 8,400 extra take-home: pension and other deductions need their own checks. Do not enter taxable pay into a calculator field asking for gross salary. The gross-to-taxable-pay guide explains that distinction.

Record timing and later adjustments

Keep the period earned separate from the payment date, especially when sales are approved after a quarter closes. Ask payroll to explain the period used for tax. If a customer later cancels, retain the original commission and the proposed reversal rather than quietly replacing the old schedule.

Check that any recovery is reflected once, with a clear explanation of earnings and deduction adjustments. For a payment covering earlier periods, use the arrears allocation checklist. For recurring commission, build a month-by-month record rather than assuming the highest month is your normal income.

What to ask before accepting a commission plan

Confirm the eligibility rules, rate, payment trigger, approval process and treatment of cancellations or departure. Ask for a sample gross calculation and a separate payroll estimate. Keep guaranteed salary apart from uncertain sales income when budgeting: tax classification cannot tell you whether a target will be achieved or a disputed commission is contractually due.

title: Check Your Workplace Pension Contributions
metaTitle: Check Your Workplace Pension Contributions | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Compare employee and employer pension contributions with your scheme statement, separate investment movements and investigate missing workplace pension credits.
content:
To check a workplace pension, compare the contribution rules and payroll entries with the amounts credited to your scheme account. A payslip deduction and an employer contribution shown for information are different entries; both need a clear destination.

This checklist concerns occupational or umbrella pension records, rather than replacing the NSSF statement guide. Use the PAYE calculator to examine the salary impact of contributions, with the tax relief guide for the supporting tax context. A calculator cannot confirm that money reached a pension fund.

Establish what should be contributed

Obtain the scheme name, membership number and the contribution terms. Check the definition of pensionable salary: it may differ from total gross pay. Identify the employee rate, employer rate and any additional voluntary contribution separately. Do not assume the employer matches every voluntary increase.

For example, suppose the scheme terms specify 5% from the employee and 10% from the employer on KES 80,000 pensionable salary. The expected amounts are KES 4,000 and KES 8,000, or KES 12,000 combined. These are illustrative contractual rates, not universal Kenyan pension rates. If the payslip also contains NSSF, identify whether that is separate or how any approved Tier II arrangement is accounted for.

Request the statement and transaction detail

RBA’s member-rights guidance includes access to annual benefit statements and scheme information. Obtain the latest dated statement through the administrator’s verified channel. If the statement only shows annual totals, request the underlying contribution periods needed to investigate a discrepancy.

Build a simple worksheet: payroll month, pensionable salary, expected employee contribution, expected employer contribution, statement credit and unresolved difference. Keep the deduction month distinct from the date a credit was posted. Ask the administrator which period an unclear transaction covers.

Separate contributions from investment movements

A balance change is not the same as a contribution total. For illustration, an opening balance of KES 200,000 plus KES 12,000 contributions and KES 2,000 net investment movement gives KES 214,000. A closing balance alone cannot show whether the employee and employer amounts were correctly allocated.

Ask how the statement presents investment returns, charges, transfers and adjustments. Avoid adding a charge twice if it is already included in a net figure. For defined-benefit arrangements, request the scheme’s benefit explanation rather than assuming the balance arithmetic of an individual contribution account applies.

Investigate a shortfall with both parties

Send payroll and the administrator the specific months and amounts. Ask payroll for remittance evidence and your entry in the schedule, with colleagues’ details removed. Ask the administrator whether the payment was received and allocated to your membership. A bulk receipt does not settle an individual allocation query.

Keep a dated query log and obtain an updated statement after correction. If the scheme cannot resolve an anomaly, use the complaint information linked from RBA’s official member-rights page. Do not send passwords or one-time codes to someone offering to repair your pension record.

Reconcile the tax record separately

Read pension contributions and PAYE for deduction limits and cash-flow trade-offs. A contribution credited to the fund does not establish that payroll applied the correct tax deduction. Conversely, a tax deduction on the payslip is not proof of remittance.

If Tier II is being routed to another scheme, review the contracting-out checklist and confirm which record should show it. Close the query only when the contribution trail and payroll explanation agree.

Once the contributions match, check how scheme fees affect the amount invested.

title: Pension Transfers When Changing Jobs
metaTitle: Pension Transfers When Changing Jobs | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Plan a Kenyan workplace pension transfer when changing employers: compare retaining and transferring benefits, prepare records and verify the receiving credit.
content:
Changing jobs does not mean you must cash out your workplace pension. RBA explains that benefits can remain invested in the former scheme or be transferred to another registered scheme, including an individual plan or a new employer’s scheme. Confirm the options and conditions for your own arrangement before signing an instruction.

The PAYE calculator can help check how new payroll contributions affect take-home pay; it does not value a pension transfer. Use the employment situations guide for the broader move between employers. This checklist concerns occupational or umbrella pension benefits, not a request to withdraw statutory NSSF balances.

Compare retaining benefits with transferring them

Start with the current administrator’s written statement of your options. RBA’s saving and membership guidance describes retaining benefits and transferring to a registered arrangement. Ask each scheme about charges, investment choices, access rules and the information you will receive.

Compare like with like: a quoted past return is not a future guarantee, and moving an account does not necessarily preserve every feature of the old scheme. Where benefits are defined by a formula or include guarantees, obtain a written explanation of what would be given up. Seek regulated advice where the decision depends on that valuation.

Prepare a transfer file

  • The old scheme name, member number and dated benefit statement.
  • The employment leaving date and final contribution period.
  • Receiving scheme registration and membership details confirmed with its administrator.
  • The official transfer forms and required identity evidence.
  • Your written instruction, acknowledgement and a named contact at each scheme.

Use verified administrator channels for financial and identity documents. Confirm payment instructions directly with the receiving scheme. Do not redirect a scheme transfer through a personal account merely because an intermediary says it is faster.

Reconcile the final contribution before transfer

Check whether the latest payslip deduction and employer contribution have reached the old scheme. A statement produced before the final payroll may not include them. Ask how late credits will be handled if the main transfer is processed first.

For example, suppose the confirmed transfer amount is KES 450,000 and a further KES 12,000 contribution is still awaiting allocation. Record the KES 12,000 as an unresolved item. Do not describe KES 462,000 as the completed transfer until the administrators confirm the amount actually sent and credited. Investment movements and charges may also change a valuation between dates.

Track the instruction through to receipt

RBA’s member-rights guidance describes a right to transfer accrued benefits to another registered scheme within sixty days of written notice, subject to the applicable statutory or regulatory period. Keep evidence of when notice was received and ask promptly about incomplete requirements. Treat an unexplained delay as a query, not as a reason to send a duplicate instruction.

Request the outgoing confirmation and incoming statement, then match the amount, reference and membership number. Keep any explanation for differences. An acknowledgement that a form was received is not proof that the receiving account has been funded.

Keep the new payroll and old benefits separate

Check the new employer’s first pension deduction independently of the transfer. The old balance and new monthly contributions are different transactions. Use the workplace contribution checklist to keep them distinct.

Keep your final payslip and tax records too: the exit payroll checklist and PAYE when changing jobs cover those separate tasks. Do not treat the transfer instruction as a new employee contribution eligible for fresh payroll relief, or assume the tax consequences of a cash withdrawal are identical to a scheme transfer. Confirm any proposed withdrawal with the administrator before choosing it.

title: Salary Advances and PAYE in Kenya
metaTitle: Salary Advances and PAYE in Kenya | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Reconcile a Kenyan salary advance with payroll: separate early cash from extra earnings, check recovery and avoid deducting the same amount twice.
content:
A salary advance changes when you receive money. It does not necessarily increase your earnings or reduce the salary on which PAYE is calculated. Before checking the tax, establish whether the payment is an advance against pay, an extra earnings payment or a separate employee loan.

Use the PAYE calculator for your ordinary salary calculation, then reconcile the advance separately. The employment situations guide explains other changes to normal payroll. A calculator cannot identify the legal nature of a payment from its bank reference.

Confirm what the payment represents

Ask payroll for the amount advanced, payment date, recovery period and written terms. Identify whether it is part of the current month's pay or will be recovered across later months. An approved advance should have a traceable balance, rather than appearing as an unexplained negative earnings entry.

KRA's 2017 employer guide, printed page 28, says ordinary salary advances are normally not taxed when advanced, with tax calculated on full pay before recovery in the recovery month. This is historical procedural guidance, not a source for today's tax bands. Use KRA's current PAYE page for the current calculation framework and ask payroll to confirm the treatment of your arrangement.

Reconcile the two bank payments

Suppose your verified net salary before advance recovery is KES 70,000. You receive KES 20,000 early, and the full advance is recovered in the same month's payroll. The remaining transfer is KES 50,000. The two transfers total KES 70,000; the advance is not an additional KES 20,000 of disposable income.

This example assumes no fees, interest or other adjustments. It deliberately starts with an already verified net figure rather than implying that KES 70,000 is the net pay for a particular gross salary. Check gross earnings, tax and other deductions first using the payslip checklist.

Keep recovery out of the wrong calculation

Do not simply reduce gross salary by the recovered advance before estimating PAYE. That confuses settlement of money already received with a qualifying tax deduction. Ask payroll to show the tax calculation separately from the advance balance and the final bank transfer.

If both an early payment and the normal full salary reach your bank, ask whether the advance remains outstanding. If payroll recovers the amount twice, send the two entries and payment references for reconciliation. Our salary overpayment guide covers the separate problem of money paid in error.

Track instalments and leaving employment

For an instalment arrangement, keep opening balance, new advances, each recovery and closing balance. For example, KES 30,000 outstanding less one KES 10,000 recovery leaves KES 20,000, assuming no further transactions. Compare the balance with the next payslip instead of restarting the schedule each month.

Before leaving a job, request the outstanding balance and proposed final-pay treatment in writing. Read the salary deduction checks; a debt balance alone does not explain every deduction an employer may make. Do not assume a disputed recovery can be settled by changing the tax figure.

When the arrangement is an employee loan

A longer-term or interest-bearing loan needs its own review. KRA's employee-loan guidance explains that below-market employer loans can create fringe benefit tax obligations for the employer. Do not apply an old illustrative interest rate to a current loan. Request the loan agreement, repayment schedule and payroll explanation before treating it as a routine salary advance.

Sources and review date

title: Company Car Private Use: Payroll Checks
metaTitle: Company Car Private Use: Payroll Checks | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check restricted private use of a company car in Kenya, prepare journey records and ask payroll for the basis of any reduced taxable benefit.
content:
A company car described as “mainly for work” does not automatically qualify for a lower taxable benefit. The useful questions are what use is actually permitted, how that restriction is evidenced, and what basis payroll has for the value it uses.

Use the PAYE calculator to understand the salary tax calculation, alongside the employer payroll guide. This checklist focuses on evidence and changes in access. For the standard valuation calculation, read the benefits-in-kind guide.

Separate a restriction from a description

KRA's employer guide, printed page 16, explains that the Commissioner determines a lower car benefit where satisfied that use is restricted. It is not permission for an employee to choose a discount based on their own mileage estimate. The guide is the 2017 edition; its old income-tax tables should not be reused for current payroll.

Ask for the written vehicle policy and the basis for the payroll treatment. Establish who can drive, whether private trips are permitted, where the vehicle is kept and how keys are controlled. Record exceptions as well as normal rules. A policy that says one thing while actual use differs needs clarification.

Build a usable vehicle-use record

A practical record can include the date, driver, journey purpose, starting and ending odometer readings and the authorising manager where relevant. Keep vehicle allocation and return dates, service periods and written changes to access alongside it. These are suggested evidence fields, not a claim that one homemade form guarantees a tax outcome.

For illustration, an odometer moving from 18,200 to 18,360 records 160 kilometres. That establishes distance, not whether every kilometre was business travel or whether a particular benefit reduction is approved. Explain missing periods rather than filling them with estimates presented as facts.

Ask payroll what supports a reduced value

  • Which vehicle and employee does the valuation cover?
  • What ownership or lease arrangement applies?
  • What restriction and supporting records were considered?
  • What determination or other documented basis supports the value used?
  • From which payroll period does that treatment apply?

Keep the response with the valuation worksheet. A colleague's car arrangement is not evidence for yours. If approval or interpretation is unresolved, ask the employer's tax adviser or KRA for the appropriate treatment instead of silently reducing the figure.

Keep taxable value separate from cash

KRA's current PAYE guidance lists employer-provided car benefits as taxable non-cash employment benefits. A benefit value is not extra cash paid into your bank, and it is not itself the tax charge.

Request a reconciliation from cash earnings to taxable income and then to bank payment. Check any separate employee payment or car charge against the agreement. Use taxable pay versus gross pay to avoid entering a non-cash value as though it were additional cash salary. Confirm how your calculator inputs handle benefits before relying on a take-home estimate.

Review changes rather than copying last month

Tell payroll when the car is replaced, returned or newly available for private use. Keep the dated handover and policy change. Do not assume a temporary absence or a weekend without driving proves that the benefit has disappeared.

Before accepting a car-based package, compare the practical value and cash effect using salary versus benefits. The right question is what the arrangement gives you and costs you, supported by an explained payroll valuation—not whether a perk sounds tax-free.

title: Pension Beneficiary Nominations in Kenya
metaTitle: Pension Beneficiary Nominations in Kenya | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Update Kenyan pension beneficiary nominations, check shares total 100%, keep acknowledgement and understand why a nomination is not a guaranteed payout.
content:
A pension beneficiary nomination tells your scheme whom you would like to receive benefits if you die. Keep it current with the scheme administrator; naming someone in an employer's emergency-contact file is not evidence that your pension nomination has been updated.

This guide concerns workplace and personal retirement schemes. Use the PAYE calculator for the salary impact of contributions and the tax relief guide for payroll context. Neither calculates a death benefit or decides who receives it. Nomination is a separate record-keeping task.

Who can you nominate?

RBA's saving and membership guidance describes nominations for people financially dependent on you or others you wish to benefit, including family members. Obtain your scheme's current form and ask the administrator how its rules apply, particularly for minors or complex family circumstances.

Do not treat a nomination as an unconditional guarantee. RBA's membership-benefits guidance states that trustees may vary a nomination on proper written grounds. If you need certainty about a disputed entitlement or succession question, get advice on the applicable rules rather than assuming a percentage written on a form settles it.

Complete a separate record for each scheme

List each pension arrangement, the administrator and your membership reference. Request a nomination form through a verified channel. Provide the identity, relationship and contact details the scheme actually asks for; do not send unnecessary identity documents to an unverified intermediary.

Check whether the form replaces all previous nominations or only changes specified details. Follow the signing, dating and submission instructions. If an online process is available, retain its confirmation. Avoid assuming a form saved on your laptop has reached the scheme.

Make the percentages add up

RBA advises that nominated shares should total 100%. For a purely illustrative allocation, 50%, 30% and 20% total 100%. Writing 50%, 30% and 30% totals 110% and needs correction. These examples are arithmetic checks, not a recommendation about how to divide your savings.

Use the current form's instructions for rounding and for any alternative nominees. Do not invent a second allocation that conflicts with the primary one. Ask the administrator how to record a beneficiary who is a child and what information would be required at claim stage.

Update after life changes

RBA specifically encourages updates after major events such as marriage, a death in the family or additional children. A change of address, contact details or scheme can also make a record worth checking. Set a review reminder alongside your annual benefit-statement review.

When changing jobs, confirm nominations with both the old and new administrators. Do not assume that transferring a pension automatically transfers the nomination form. Use the pension-transfer checklist to track the money separately from the beneficiary record.

Keep proof without sharing account access

Retain a dated copy and acknowledgement identifying the scheme. If the administrator confirms an update by message, save it with the version submitted. Ask for confirmation of unclear or rejected entries; a submission receipt alone may not mean every field was accepted.

Tell a trusted person how to identify your schemes and reach their official administrators, without sharing passwords or one-time codes. Keep contribution statements accurate through the workplace pension checklist. A nomination cannot correct missing contributions, and a current statement cannot prove your chosen beneficiary details are on file.

Does changing a nominee change PAYE?

The nomination itself is not a new pension contribution or a payroll tax-relief claim. Keep it separate from any request to change savings contributions. For that separate decision, read pension contributions and take-home pay, then send payroll the relevant contribution instructions.

Sources and review date

Published and reviewed on 5 November 2026. Use the rules and scheme instructions applicable to your circumstances. Historical guidance is identified where used.

title: Employer Medical Cover on a Kenyan Payslip
metaTitle: Employer Medical Cover on a Kenyan Payslip | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check who paid the premium, distinguish group cover from a cash allowance, and reconcile a family medical top-up with your Kenyan payslip.
content:
Your offer says “medical cover”, but your payslip shows a medical deduction. Both can be right: the employer may buy your base cover while you pay extra to add a dependant. First establish who paid whom. The premium, the annual treatment limit and the amount taken from your salary are three different numbers.

Did you receive money or insurance?

For an ordinary full-time employee with qualifying employer-paid medical insurance, KRA lists the employer cover as not chargeable to PAYE. A fixed medical allowance paid to you as unrestricted cash is ordinarily taxable cash pay. Enter a cash allowance with your earnings in the PAYE calculator; do not add your policy’s hospital limit as monthly salary. If the arrangement is a reimbursement, or you are a director, ask payroll for the basis specific to that arrangement.

Follow one premium through the payslip

Suppose the company pays KSh 48,000 a year directly to the insurer. You elect a family upgrade costing you KSh 1,500 a month. The base premium works out at KSh 4,000 a month for budgeting, but that amount does not leave your bank account. Over twelve months your own share is KSh 18,000. Start with that share when checking deductions, not the combined KSh 66,000 cost.

Find the first month of the upgrade and count actual deductions. If you joined in July, six deductions of KSh 1,500 through December total KSh 9,000. Compare that figure with the premium confirmation for the same months. An annual renewal invoice may cover a different period.

Check relief separately from cover

Being insured is not itself proof that you paid a premium. For your own share, check the policy, covered person and proof of payment against the insurance relief requirements. Do not claim the employer-funded share as your own. A statutory SHIF deduction is a separate payslip item; check your SHA contributions independently of the private policy.

What to request if the figures differ

Ask HR for the cover start date and the employer/employee split. Ask payroll whether the line represents cash earnings, a deduction from net pay, or a benefit displayed for information. If it is a deduction, ask for the months and people it covers. A renewal paid in one instalment can look like a duplicate until those periods are identified. Share premium records, not medical diagnoses. Use the employment guide if a change of job altered your cover dates.

Sources and review date

title: Pension Scheme Fees in Kenya: What to Ask
metaTitle: Pension Scheme Fees in Kenya: What to Ask | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Compare pension charges in shillings, distinguish fees on contributions from fees on balances, and check whether a quoted return already includes costs.
content:
A charge of 1% on a contribution and a charge of 1% on a pension balance have the same headline rate but can cost very different amounts. To compare Kenyan pension schemes, ask for the fee basis, the period and the amount in shillings at your actual balance.

Start with the type of pension

The Retirement Benefits Authority’s scheme guide distinguishes defined contribution schemes, where contributions and investment performance matter to the member’s pot, from defined benefit schemes, which calculate benefits using a formula. The comparison below is for a defined contribution account. For a defined benefit promise, ask the administrator for the benefit formula and your accrued entitlement instead of trying to reconstruct it from a fee percentage.

Put each charge on the same basis

Request the dated fee schedule for your specific plan. For each charge, write down the rate, what it applies to, when it is taken and who pays it. For example, is an administration fee paid separately by your employer, deducted from each deposit, or met out of scheme assets? If a rate applies to assets, ask whether the calculation uses a daily, average or closing balance. Check whether any stated fixed minimum changes the result on a small pot.

In an illustrative year you contribute KSh 5,000 each month. One per cent of those twelve deposits is KSh 600. In a different arrangement, 1% of an assumed average balance of KSh 400,000 is KSh 4,000. The second figure is not KSh 600 simply because the monthly contribution is unchanged. These are examples of different charging bases, not Kenyan tariffs or a forecast. Ask both schemes to cost the same balance and contribution pattern.

Is the quoted return before or after fees?

If a statement credits KSh 16,000 of investment income after a management charge, subtracting that charge again understates the balance. Ask which costs are already reflected in the credited return and which appear as separate debits. Reconcile opening balance plus deposits and credited income, less separate withdrawals and debits, to the closing balance. Use the contribution statement check for a missing deposit before classifying the shortfall as a fee.

Keep the payroll decision separate

Use the PAYE calculator for the salary effect of a qualifying contribution; it does not project scheme fees or investment returns. The tax relief guide explains the payroll side. Before moving an existing pot, get a transfer quotation showing any one-off costs and the amount expected to arrive. The pension transfer checklist helps match the outgoing amount to the receiving statement.

Sources and review date

Reviewed 6 November 2026. RBA explains scheme designs and provider roles; your own scheme’s current documents are the source for its actual charges.

title: Staff Meals and PAYE in Kenya
metaTitle: Staff Meals and PAYE in Kenya | PAYE Calculator Kenya
metaDescription: Check the PAYE treatment of canteen meals and cash lunch allowances in Kenya, with an example showing the meal value above the monthly exclusion.
content:
If an employer provides qualifying staff meals worth KSh 6,400 in a month, the whole KSh 6,400 does not become taxable simply because the value exceeds KSh 5,000. The first KSh 5,000 is excluded; in this example KSh 1,400 goes into taxable employment income. That KSh 1,400 is the value to tax, not the PAYE bill.

Which meal arrangement are you checking?

Start with what the employee actually receives. Meals served in the employer’s canteen are straightforward to identify. If a caterer provides the meals, document the contract, supplier’s taxpayer registration and the employees served. If staff instead receive unrestricted money with their salary, treat the ordinary cash lunch allowance as cash pay: the meal exclusion is not a general tax-free allowance for buying food. For travel expenses, establish the separate travel arrangement rather than applying this canteen example.

Calculate the employee’s monthly meal value

Suppose payroll’s supported value per employer-funded lunch is KSh 320 and the employee receives 20 lunches. The total is KSh 6,400. Apply the KSh 5,000 monthly exclusion once across that employee’s qualifying meals, leaving KSh 1,400. If the employee receives only 12 lunches at the same value, KSh 3,840 is within the exclusion. Do not deduct the unused KSh 1,160 from their salary income.

The KRA notice implementing the December 2024 change sets out the first KSh 60,000 annually, expressed as KSh 5,000 monthly. KRA’s current PAYE guidance separately identifies the excess as a non-cash benefit. For a mixed invoice covering staff, guests and several months, first establish a defensible employee and period allocation. Dividing the entire bill by this month’s headcount could include meals the employee never received.

Why the bank payment does not rise by the meal value

The employee has already received lunch. A taxable non-cash amount can affect PAYE without creating a second payment for the meal. Use the PAYE calculator for a cash-salary baseline, then ask payroll to show the meal addition in its taxable-pay calculation. Entering the entire catering bill as extra gross cash would misstate take-home pay. See taxable pay versus gross pay for how to read the two figures.

What to keep with the calculation

Keep the supplier invoice, period covered, meal count, valuation basis and any employee payments together. If an employee pays part of the price or uses a voucher with several redemption options, confirm what was funded and the basis for the treatment before using the simple fully funded example. Use the employer payroll guide to place the calculation in your monthly review and the salary allowance guide for cash alternatives.

Sources and review date

title: Mileage Reimbursements and PAYE in Kenya
content:
A mileage reimbursement can contain both an expense repayment and a taxable excess. To check your Kenyan payslip, reconcile three things: the approved business kilometres, the rate used to pay you and the rate payroll used for tax. A line labelled “mileage” does not explain those figures by itself.

Use the PAYE calculator for your ordinary salary baseline, then ask payroll to show how the taxable mileage excess changes that calculation. The calculator does not decide whether a journey qualifies or supply an AA mileage tariff.

Which part of a mileage claim is taxable?

KRA's PAYE guidance says mileage reimbursement above AA Kenya rates is taxable on the employee, effective 1 July 2023. The Finance Act 2023, section 5 connects the reimbursement treatment to travel on official duties and the Automobile Association of Kenya's standard mileage rate.

Start by distinguishing your own-car business journey from a fixed transport allowance, a personal trip or use of an employer's car. Those are different arrangements. See how salary allowances are taxed and the separate company-car private-use checks. Do not assume a normal commute qualifies merely because you drove to work.

Reconcile the claim before checking the tax

  1. List the journeys. Record date, origin, destination, business purpose, kilometres claimed and the approving manager. Explain detours rather than silently increasing the distance.
  2. Check the vehicle and period. Ask payroll for the applicable AA schedule or rate evidence, including the vehicle details and date used. An old colleague's rate is not reliable evidence for your claim.
  3. Separate the employer's payment policy. Your employer may pay a different rate. Obtain both that policy rate and the tax comparison rate; they answer different questions.
  4. Match approval to payment. Reconcile approved kilometres to the expense payment, payslip or bank credit. Exclude rejected or duplicated journeys from your reconciliation.
  5. Trace the taxable excess. Ask which payroll period and taxable-pay line contains it. If expenses were paid separately, the taxable element may still appear in payroll.

Worked example: payment versus taxable excess

Suppose 200 business kilometres are approved. The employer pays KES 75 per kilometre, while the applicable comparison rate is assumed to be KES 60. Both rates here are invented solely to demonstrate the arithmetic; they are not published AA Kenya rates.

  • Payment: 200 × KES 75 = KES 15,000.
  • Comparison amount: 200 × KES 60 = KES 12,000.
  • Excess for payroll to assess: KES 15,000 − KES 12,000 = KES 3,000.

KES 3,000 is a taxable-income amount in this example, not the PAYE bill. The eventual tax depends on the employee's full tax calculation. Equally, adding the entire KES 15,000 to taxable pay would not reflect this assumed split. Check the distinction between taxable pay and gross pay before comparing totals.

What to send payroll when the figures differ

Send the claim reference, approved journey log, payment proof and a small reconciliation showing your figures beside payroll's. Ask for the rate source, taxable excess and period of recognition in writing. Keep fuel receipts or other supporting evidence required by your employer, but do not treat a fuel receipt alone as proof of the mileage rate or business purpose.

If a claim includes a fuel advance, ask how it was offset so the same cost is not reimbursed twice. If you find an error after processing, request an explanation of the correction and retain the revised payslip or expense statement. Do not adjust your own annual tax figures from a guessed rate.

What if the employer pays below the AA rate?

A lower payment does not by itself establish an employment entitlement to the difference. Review the agreed expense policy and approved claim with your employer. The tax comparison and what the employer agreed to reimburse are separate questions.

The employment and tax guide puts this check alongside other changes to monthly pay.

Sources and review date

Reviewed 7 November 2026 against KRA's PAYE guidance and the enacted Finance Act 2023 linked above. This article supplies a reconciliation method, not a current AA tariff.
